definition_zh: 不幸的；倒霉的；不吉利的；不凑巧的
definition_en: having bad luck, or believed to bring bad luck
core_image: 刚打出的一手好牌，最后却被人一分反超
scene: 他赶到车站时，车刚刚开走，地面上还留着轮印。 He was unlucky to miss the last train.
sceneCN: 这里 unlucky 是「倒霉的」（第 1 个义项：运气不好）；句意为他赶上末班车算是运气不好。好牌却被反超，正是这个词的核心画面。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「不幸地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「不幸；倒霉」
去掉否定前缀的形容词，义为「幸运的」
词族核心名词，义为「运气」

senses.title: Hit by bad luck
senses.definition: suffering from bad luck that no one could have prevented
senses.definitionCN: 碰上谁都避免不了的不顺
senses.example: He was unlucky to lose on the last point.
senses.exampleCN: 他在最后一分上输了，实在倒霉。
senses.why: The prefix negates lucky, and luck came into English from Dutch as a word for chance.
senses.whyCN: 前缀否定了 lucky，而 luck 由荷兰语进入英语，本指机遇。

senses.title: In an unlucky situation
senses.definition: used with in to describe a field where luck has gone against someone
senses.definitionCN: 与 in 连用，说明某方面运气不济
senses.example: He has always been unlucky in business.
senses.exampleCN: 他做生意一直运气不佳。
senses.why: Chance can favour one part of life and betray another, which the phrase with in marks.
senses.whyCN: 机遇会偏爱生活的某一方面而背弃另一面，与 in 连用正标记这一点。

senses.title: Bad luck at the wrong moment
senses.definition: used of a small accident of timing that spoils a plan
senses.definitionCN: 形容恰好毁掉计划的小小时间差
senses.example: An unlucky step sent the tray to the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 脚下不凑巧一步，托盘就摔到了地上。
senses.why: Small accidents are the smallest pieces of chance, and the word covers them too.
senses.whyCN: 小意外是机遇最小的碎片，这个词同样涵盖。

senses.title: Believed to bring bad fortune
senses.definition: used of numbers, days, or objects that people think carry bad luck
senses.definitionCN: 形容人们认为带着厄运的数字、日子或器物
senses.example: In many buildings the unlucky floor number is left out.
senses.exampleCN: 许多楼里会跳过那个不吉利的楼层号。
senses.why: From bad luck that happens to bad luck that is said to come, the word widens its reach.
senses.whyCN: 从「碰上的坏运」到「据说会来的坏运」，这个词扩大了应用范围。

senses.title: A person who deserves sympathy
senses.definition: used of someone whose bad luck is not their own fault
senses.definitionCN: 形容运气不佳而非自作自受的人
senses.example: The unlucky passengers queued again for the next flight.
senses.exampleCN: 那些倒霉的乘客又排队等下一班飞机。
senses.why: Chance strikes without blame, and the word often carries a note of sympathy.
senses.whyCN: 机遇的打击无关过错，因此这个词常带着同情的意味。

intro.en: Luck entered English from Low German or Dutch in the sixteenth century, and unlucky followed.
intro.cn: luck 十六世纪由低地德语或荷兰语进入英语，unlucky 随之出现。

items.en: Luc or luk meant good fortune in the gambling sense.
items.cn: luc 或 luk 在赌博语境中意为好运。

items.en: English borrowed luck and quickly used it for chance in general.
items.cn: 英语借入 luck，很快用来泛指机遇。

items.en: Unlucky was formed by adding the negative prefix to lucky.
items.cn: lucky 加否定前缀形成 unlucky。

items.en: The word extended to numbers, days, and objects thought to bring harm.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到被认为招祸的数字、日子与器物。

items.en: It remains the everyday word for a chance victim.
items.cn: 至今它仍指被机运击中的人。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers luck words, and the near-meaning group covers misfortune words.
note.cn: 形近组收集 luck 词族，近义组覆盖表示不幸的词。

entries.definitionCN: 不太可能的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

normalIntro.en: One prefix denies luck, and the word runs from a lost point to a number nobody prints.
normalIntro.cn: 一个前缀否定了运气，从丢的一分一直到没人印出的数字。

normal.en: Un- plus lucky: not favoured by chance.
normal.cn: un- 加 lucky：没被机遇眷顾。

normal.en: Be unlucky to do is the pattern for bad breaks.
normal.cn: be unlucky to do 是形容倒霉事的常用句型。

normal.en: Unlucky in love is a fixed phrase with in.
normal.cn: unlucky in love 是与 in 连用的固定说法。

normal.en: Luck came from Dutch, so it is not a Latin word.
normal.cn: luck 来自荷兰语，并不是拉丁语词。

normal.en: Unluckily is the adverb; unfortunately is more formal.
normal.cn: 副词是 unluckily，unfortunately 更正式。

abstract.en: Picture a good hand of cards beaten by one point.
abstract.cn: 想象一手好牌被一分反超。

abstract.en: See a train leaving as you reach the platform.
abstract.cn: 看火车在你跑上站台时开走。

abstract.en: See a lift panel with one number missing.
abstract.cn: 看电梯按钮上缺了一个数字。

examples.en: The unlucky driver was hit from behind twice in one week.
examples.cn: 那位倒霉的司机一周里被追尾两次。

examples.en: Thirteen is thought unlucky in some countries.
examples.cn: 十三个一些国家被认为不吉利。

examples.en: Unluckily, the rain began exactly at the ceremony.
examples.cn: 不幸的是，雨恰好在仪式开始时下了起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺落地记」——俺一落地就挨记一下，走了才有脚印，真倒霉。

root: 前缀 un-（不）+ lucky，luck 于十六世纪自低地德语或荷兰语 luc/luk（好运）进入英语

sensesIntro.en: One denial of chance covers a lost match, a wrong moment, a forbidden number, and a sympathetically late passenger.
sensesIntro.cn: 一次对机遇的否定，覆盖输掉的比赛、错的时刻、被忌讳的数字与令人同情的晚到乘客。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a strong hand beaten by a single point.
core.cn: 核心意象：一手好牌被一分反超。

branches.en: The break branch: losing on the last point.
branches.cn: 运气分支：在最后一分上输掉。

branches.en: The life-area branch: luck that fails in one field.
branches.cn: 生活领域分支：某一方面运气不济。

branches.en: The timing branch: a step taken half a second early.
branches.cn: 时机分支：早了半秒的一步。

branches.en: The omen branch: numbers and days said to bring harm.
branches.cn: 预兆分支：据说招祸的数字与日子。

branches.en: The sympathy branch: the passenger who did nothing wrong.
branches.cn: 同情分支：毫无过错的乘客。

intro.en: A negative prefix on an adjective that English borrowed from Dutch.
intro.cn: 否定前缀压在一个借自荷兰语的形容词上。

latinIntro.en: Luck is not Latin, so the Latin list is empty for this word.
latinIntro.cn: luck 并非拉丁语词，因此这个词的拉丁词条留空。

items.example: An ill-fated voyage lost three ships.
items.exampleCN: 一次注定不祥的航行失了三艘船。

items.example: The plan was doomed from the start.
items.exampleCN: 这计划从一开始就注定失败。

definition_en: to stop or delay something, or to hang something from above
core_image: 钟摆从上方垂下，停在半空中
scene: 比赛因大雨暂停了。 The match was suspended because of heavy rain.
sceneCN: 这里 suspend 是「暂停」（第 1 个义项）；句意：比赛因大雨暂停了。

senses.title: To stop temporarily
senses.definition: to stop something for a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 使某事停止一段时间
senses.example: The match was suspended because of heavy rain.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛因大雨暂停了。
senses.why: This is the common sense of a temporary stop.
senses.whyCN: 这是「暂时停止」的常见义项。

senses.title: To hang from above
senses.definition: to hang something so that it is held from above
senses.definitionCN: 把某物从上吊起
senses.example: A lamp was suspended from the ceiling.
senses.exampleCN: 一盏灯悬挂在天花板上。
senses.why: This is the original physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最初的物理义项。

senses.title: To remove someone temporarily
senses.definition: to make someone leave their job or school for a time
senses.definitionCN: 使某人暂时离开工作或学校
senses.example: He was suspended from school for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 他被停学一周。
senses.why: Here the stopping applies to a person's position.
senses.whyCN: 这里停止的是人的职位。

intro.en: Suspend joins Latin words for under and hanging.
intro.cn: suspend 把拉丁语中表示「在下」和「悬挂」的词结合起来。

items.en: Sub meant under.
items.cn: sub 意为在下。

items.en: Pendere meant to hang.
items.cn: pendere 意为悬挂。

items.en: Suspendere meant to hang up.
items.cn: suspendere 意为吊起。

items.en: Suspendre meant to hang or delay.
items.cn: suspendre 意为悬挂或推迟。

items.en: Suspend meant to stop or hang.
items.cn: suspend 意为停止或悬挂。

note.en: Suspend is compared with look-alike words and with words for stopping.
note.cn: 把 suspend 与形近词以及表示停止的词作比较。

entries.definition: to move to a later time

normalIntro.en: Suspend means to hold something up or hold it back.
normalIntro.cn: suspend 意为把某物吊起，或把某事按住。

normal.en: The match was suspended because of heavy rain.
normal.cn: 比赛因大雨暂停了。

normal.en: A lamp was suspended from the ceiling.
normal.cn: 一盏灯悬挂在天花板上。

normal.en: He was suspended from school for a week.
normal.cn: 他被停学一周。

normal.en: The airline suspended all flights.
normal.cn: 航空公司暂停了所有航班。

normal.en: They suspended judgement until the facts were clear.
normal.cn: 在事实清楚之前他们暂缓判断。

abstract.en: Suspension is time held in the air before it falls again.
abstract.cn: 暂停是时间悬在空中，等待再次落下。

abstract.en: The same word holds a lamp and holds back a decision.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既吊着灯，也按住决定。

abstract.en: To suspend is to interrupt without ending.
abstract.cn: 暂停是打断而不终结。

examples.en: The match was suspended because of heavy rain.
examples.cn: 比赛因大雨暂停了。

examples.en: A lamp was suspended from the ceiling.
examples.cn: 一盏灯悬挂在天花板上。

examples.en: He was suspended from school for a week.
examples.cn: 他被停学一周。

dict_mnemonic.text: sub 表示「在下」，pend 表示「悬挂」，suspend 就是吊在下面，引申为把某事「挂起」即暂停。

root: 源自拉丁语 suspendere（sub 在下 + pendere 悬挂），经古法语 suspendre 进入英语，由悬挂引申为暂停。

sensesIntro.en: Suspend means to stop something temporarily, to hang it, or to remove someone for a time.
sensesIntro.cn: suspend 指暂时停止、悬挂，或使某人暂时离职停学。

core.en: Holding something up, or holding it back.
core.cn: 把某物吊起，或把某事按住。

branches.en: The match was suspended because of heavy rain.
branches.cn: 比赛因大雨暂停了。

branches.en: The airline suspended all flights.
branches.cn: 航空公司暂停了所有航班。

branches.en: A lamp was suspended from the ceiling.
branches.cn: 一盏灯悬挂在天花板上。

branches.en: He was suspended from school for a week.
branches.cn: 他被停学一周。

branches.en: A hanging lamp and a paused match share one verb.
branches.cn: 吊着的灯与暂停的比赛共用一个动词。

intro.en: Suspend forms suspension, suspender, and the participle suspended.
intro.cn: suspend 可构成 suspension、suspender 与分词 suspended。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pendere also appears in pendant, depend, and pendulum.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pendere 也出现在 pendant、depend 与 pendulum 中。

latinEntries.example: Pendere is the hanging root of suspend.
latinEntries.exampleCN: pendere 是 suspend 的「悬挂」词根。

definition_en: correctly, or for a good and fair reason
core_image: 举杯庆祝团队成果的成员
scene: 她理所当然地为团队的努力感到自豪。 She rightly felt proud of her team's effort.
sceneCN: 这里 rightly 是「理所当然地」（第 2 个义项：有充分正当理由地）；句意：她理所当然地为团队的努力感到自豪。

senses.title: Correctly
senses.definition: in a correct way
senses.definitionCN: 以正确的方式
senses.example: He rightly guessed the answer.
senses.exampleCN: 他正确地猜出了答案。
senses.why: The adverb keeps the straight, correct sense of right.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词保留了 right 笔直、正确的含义。

senses.title: With good reason
senses.definition: justifiably or fairly
senses.definitionCN: 有正当理由地；公平地
senses.example: She rightly refused the unfair offer.
senses.exampleCN: 她理所当然地拒绝了这个不公平的提议。
senses.why: A straight claim deserves a straight answer.
senses.whyCN: 正当的诉求理应得到正当的回应。

intro.en: Rightly is right plus -ly, carrying the old sense of straight and just.
intro.cn: rightly 是 right 加 -ly，承袭了笔直与公正的旧义。

items.en: Rihtlice means rightly or justly.
items.cn: rihtlice 意为正确地或公正地。

items.en: Right keeps the adjective sense.
items.cn: right 保留了形容词义。

items.en: -ly turns it into an adverb.
items.cn: -ly 把它变成副词。

items.en: Rightly often adds praise or justification.
items.cn: rightly 常带有赞许或正当理由。

items.en: Rightly so becomes a common phrase.
items.cn: rightly so 成为常用短语。

note.en: Rightly means with reason; correctly means without error.
note.cn: rightly 强调有理由，correctly 强调没有错误。

normalIntro.en: Rightly is right turned into an adverb.
normalIntro.cn: rightly 就是 right 变成的副词。

normal.en: Rightly so means it is fair to think so.
normal.cn: rightly so 意为这样想是公平的。

normal.en: Quite rightly means with full reason.
normal.cn: quite rightly 意为完全有理由。

normal.en: Rightly called means named correctly.
normal.cn: rightly called 意为被正确地称呼。

normal.en: Rightly proud means proud for good reason.
normal.cn: rightly proud 意为有理由感到自豪。

normal.en: The -ly ending makes it an adverb.
normal.cn: -ly 结尾使它成为副词。

abstract.en: Picture a judge nodding at a fair claim.
abstract.cn: 想象法官对正当的诉求点头。

abstract.en: Imagine a straight arrow finding the centre.
abstract.cn: 想象一支笔直的箭射中中心。

abstract.en: Think of applause that everyone agrees on.
abstract.cn: 想象全场都认同的掌声。

examples.en: They rightly complained about the noise.
examples.cn: 他们理所当然地抱怨了噪音。

examples.en: The city is rightly famous for its gardens.
examples.cn: 这座城市以花园闻名，实至名归。

examples.en: She rightly pointed out the mistake.
examples.cn: 她正确地指出了这个错误。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「right（对）＋ ly」——以正确而正当的方式，就是理所当然地。

root: right（笔直、公正）＋ -ly（方式副词）→ rightly，核心义「以正确而正当的方式」。

sensesIntro.en: Rightly means correctly, or with a fair and good reason.
sensesIntro.cn: rightly 意为正确地，或有公平正当的理由。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fair claim met with agreement.
core.cn: 核心意象：正当的诉求得到认同。

branches.en: Doing it correctly is the first sense.
branches.cn: 正确地做是第一个义项。

branches.en: Having a good reason is the second sense.
branches.cn: 有正当理由是第二个义项。

branches.en: A correct step and a fair step both follow the straight line.
branches.cn: 正确的举动与公平的举动都沿着直线。

branches.en: Praise is often both correct and deserved.
branches.cn: 赞许往往既正确又应得。

branches.en: Rightly so marks a deserved reaction.
branches.cn: rightly so 标记一种应得的反应。

intro.en: Rightly is right plus the adverb suffix -ly.
intro.cn: rightly 是 right 加副词后缀 -ly。

latinIntro.en: The Latin cousin rectus, straight, also lies behind correct.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语近亲 rectus（笔直）也藏在 correct 背后。

definition_en: a person who studies or writes about the fundamental questions of existence, knowledge, ethics and meaning
core_image: 一个人站在市集边，被一个简单问题绊住，越想越停不下来
scene: 雅典的廊柱下，一位老人拦住过路的人，只问什么才算好的生活。 The philosopher wrote nothing down, yet his questions were repeated for centuries.
sceneCN: 这里是「哲学家」（第 1 个义项：研究根本问题的人）；句意为这位哲学家没有写下任何著作，他的问题却被后人重复了数百年。图中可辨识物件：石柱、市集、空着的双手。

collocations.zh: 自然哲学家；早期科学家

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语 philos（爱）与 sophia（智慧）复合，指哲学
由 philosophy 加 -ic 构成，义为「哲学的；哲理性的」
由 philosophy 加 -ize 构成，义为「作哲学思考；空谈哲理」

senses.title: A student of fundamental questions
senses.definition: a person who examines existence, knowledge, ethics and meaning in a systematic, reasoned way
senses.definitionCN: 以系统、讲理的方式考察存在、知识、伦理与意义的人
senses.example: She read every Greek philosopher she could find.
senses.exampleCN: 她读遍了她能找到的每一位希腊哲学家。
senses.why: Greek philosophos was a compound meaning lover of wisdom, and the word entered English as the name of the person devoted to reasoned inquiry rather than to any particular answer.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 philosophos 是个复合词，意为「爱智慧的人」；它进入英语时指的是投身于讲理探究的人，而不是持有某个特定答案的人，所以第一个义项落在「以论证追问根本问题的人」。

senses.title: Someone calm and detached in trouble
senses.definition: a person who stays calm and reasonable when things go wrong, as if viewing life from a distance
senses.definitionCN: 遇到不顺仍保持平静与理性、仿佛从远处看待生活的人
senses.example: He lost his job and took it like a philosopher.
senses.exampleCN: 他丢了工作，却像个想得开的人那样接受了。
senses.why: If the thinker's trade is to see events in a larger frame, then anyone who keeps perspective in misfortune is said to behave like one, and the comparison hardened into a sense of its own.
senses.whyCN: 既然思想者的本行是把事情放进更大的框架里看，那么任何在逆境中仍能保持分寸的人，都可以说「像个哲学家那样」；这个比喻用久了，就独立成一个义项。

senses.title: An early investigator of nature
senses.titleCN: 自然哲学家；早期的科学家
senses.definition: the old title for a scholar who studied nature by observation and argument, before the word scientist existed
senses.definitionCN: 在「科学家」一词出现之前，对以观察和论证研究自然的学者的旧称
senses.example: Newton was still called a natural philosopher in his own time.
senses.exampleCN: 牛顿在世时仍被称为自然哲学家。
senses.why: Before the nineteenth century, questions about motion, matter and life belonged to philosophy, so the person asking them carried this title, and the sense survives in the fixed phrase natural philosopher.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪以前，关于运动、物质与生命的问题都归在哲学名下，追问这些问题的人自然带着这个头衔；这个义项如今只活在 natural philosopher 这个固定说法里。

intro.en: Philosopher is a Greek compound of loving and wise that reached English through Latin and French, and it still names a lover rather than an owner of wisdom.
intro.cn: philosopher 是希腊语中「爱」与「智慧」的复合词，经拉丁语和法语传入英语；它至今称的是智慧的爱者，而不是拥有者。

items.en: Greek philos meant loving or dear, and it marked the affection a seeker felt for what he pursued.
items.cn: 希腊语 philos 意为「爱的、亲爱的」，标记的是追寻者对所追之物的亲近之情。

items.en: Greek sophos meant wise, and sophia meant wisdom, a skill of seeing clearly rather than a store of facts.
items.cn: 希腊语 sophos 意为有智慧的，sophia 意为智慧；那是一种看清楚的能耐，而不是一堆事实。

items.en: Put together, philosophos named the lover of wisdom, a word used for thinkers such as Pythagoras and Plato.
items.cn: 两者合起来，philosophos 指「爱智慧的人」，曾被用于毕达哥拉斯、柏拉图这样的思想家。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word as philosophus, and Old French reshaped it as philosophe before English took it over.
items.cn: 拉丁语把希腊词借作 philosophus，古法语又把它改写为 philosophe，随后英语接手。

items.en: Middle English philosopher first meant an expert in the liberal arts, and modern English narrowed it back to the person who reasons about first principles.
items.cn: 中古英语的 philosopher 起初指通晓自由技艺的学者，现代英语又把它收窄回「就根本原理进行推理的人」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same love-of-wisdom stem; the near-meaning group gathers other names for people who think for a living.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「爱智慧」词干上的词；近义组收其他以思考为业者的称呼。

entries.definition: The field of study that a philosopher works in.
entries.definitionCN: 哲学家所从事的研究领域；哲学。

entries.definition: Relating to philosophy, or showing calm reasoning.
entries.definitionCN: 与哲学有关的，或表现出冷静推理的。

entries.definition: To reason or speculate in the manner of a philosopher.
entries.definitionCN: 以哲学家的方式推理或思辨。

entries.definition: The study of language and texts, built on the same Greek word for love.
entries.definitionCN: 研究语言与文献的学问，建立在同一个表示「爱」的希腊词上。

entries.definition: A person known for serious thought.
A very wise old person, often with a calm manner.
entries.definitionCN: 极为睿智的长者，常带沉静气质。

entries.definition: A person with deep academic knowledge.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有深厚学术知识的人。

entries.definition: A person who builds abstract explanations rather than practical ones.
entries.definitionCN: 构建抽象解释而非实务方案的人。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Greek compound whose two halves are still readable, and its family shows the field, the person and the activity side by side.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是希腊语复合词，两半至今可读；它的同族词把领域、人与活动并排摆在一起。

normal.en: Philosopher is philos plus sophos: a lover of wisdom, not a holder of wisdom.
normal.cn: philosopher 是 philos 加 sophos：爱智慧的人，而不是拥有智慧的人。

normal.en: The ending looks like an English agent suffix but is not: it came through Latin philosophus from Greek philosophos.
normal.cn: 词尾看着像英语的「做某事者」后缀，其实不是：它经拉丁语 philosophus 来自希腊语 philosophos。

normal.en: Philosophy is the field, philosopher the person, and philosophize the activity, all on the same Greek base.
normal.cn: philosophy 是领域，philosopher 是人，philosophize 是活动，三者共用同一个希腊词根。

normal.en: Natural philosopher is the old name for a scientist, which is why Newton appears under that title in older books.
normal.cn: natural philosopher 是科学家的旧称，所以旧书里牛顿会顶着这个头衔出现。

normal.en: The phrase 「took it like a philosopher」 turns the job title into a description of calm, and the two uses live side by side.
normal.cn: 「took it like a philosopher」这个说法把头衔变成了对镇定的描述，两种用法至今并存。

abstract.en: Imagine a man who keeps asking why until the market closes around him: that stubborn wonder is the whole word.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人不停追问为什么，直到市集在他身边收摊：那种不肯停的惊奇就是这个词的全部。

abstract.en: A philosopher owns no instrument except a question, and yet the question can outlast empires.
abstract.cn: 哲学家没有别的工具，只有一个问题；然而问题可以比帝国活得更久。

abstract.en: The word calls this person a lover, not an owner, which quietly admits that wisdom is always still ahead.
abstract.cn: 这个词称他为「爱者」而非「拥有者」，等于悄悄承认：智慧始终还在前面。

examples.en: She read every Greek philosopher she could find.
examples.cn: 她读遍了她能找到的每一位希腊哲学家。

examples.en: He lost his job and took it like a philosopher.
examples.cn: 他丢了工作，却像个想得开的人那样接受了。

examples.en: The philosopher spent the evening asking what justice really means.
examples.cn: 这位哲学家花了一整晚追问正义到底是什么。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费了索福」——费尽心思去思索幸福，越想越像个哲学家；philosopher 是哲学家。

root: 希腊语 philos（爱）加 sophos（智慧）构成 philosophos（爱智者），经拉丁语 philosophus、古法语 philosophe 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the person devoted to reasoned inquiry; from it come the everyday sense of a calm character and the older title for a student of nature.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是献身于讲理探究的人；由此分出「遇事达观的人」这一日常义，以及研究自然的学者这一旧称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person stopped in a busy market by a question that will not let go.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人在市集里被一个甩不掉的问题拦住了脚步。

branches.en: a teacher walking with students under a colonnade
branches.cn: 老师带着学生在柱廊下边走边谈

branches.en: a page of questions with no final answer
branches.cn: 写满问题却没有最终答案的一页纸

branches.en: a man shrugging at bad news and pouring tea
branches.cn: 一个人听到坏消息耸耸肩，继续倒茶

branches.en: an old book calling Newton a natural philosopher
branches.cn: 一本旧书把牛顿称作自然哲学家

branches.en: the same calm face, first as method and then as manner
branches.cn: 同一张平静的脸，先是方法，后是气质

intro.en: The word is a Greek compound of loving and wise, carried into English through Latin and French with its Greek shape almost intact.
intro.cn: 这个词是希腊语中「爱」与「智慧」的复合词，经拉丁语和法语传入英语，几乎完整保留了希腊形态。

latinIntro.en: There is no native Latin root behind this word: Latin philosophus is itself a borrowing from Greek, so no separate Latin cognate is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后没有本土拉丁词根：拉丁语 philosophus 本身就是从希腊语借来的，因此不另列拉丁同族词。

items.meaningCN: 哲学；研究根本原理的学问

definition_en: extremely impressive to look at, or surprisingly great
core_image: 烟花在河面上空同时炸开，光映在成千上万张仰起的脸上
scene: 烟花在河面上空绽放，景象十分壮观。 Fireworks burst over the river in a spectacular display.
sceneCN: 这里 spectacular 是「壮观的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：烟花在河面上空绽放，景象十分壮观。

senses.title: Impressive to see
senses.definition: extremely impressive or beautiful to look at
senses.definitionCN: 看上去极其壮观或美丽
senses.example: Fireworks burst over the river in a spectacular display.
senses.exampleCN: 烟花在河面上空绽放，景象十分壮观。
senses.why: This is the central sense of a sight worth watching.
senses.whyCN: 这是值得观看的景象的核心含义。

senses.title: Surprisingly great
senses.definition: surprisingly large or successful
senses.definitionCN: 大得或成功得出人意料
senses.example: The team made a spectacular comeback.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍实现了惊人的逆转。
senses.why: A result can be as striking as a show.
senses.whyCN: 结果也能像表演一样引人注目。

senses.title: A brilliant show
senses.definition: very exciting and well done, as a performance
senses.definitionCN: 表演非常激动人心、完成得出色
senses.example: The show ended with a spectacular finale.
senses.exampleCN: 演出以精彩的终场结束。
senses.why: The theatre gave the word its sense of a great show.
senses.whyCN: 戏剧赋予这个词「精彩演出」的含义。

intro.en: Spectacular came from Latin spectare, to look at, through spectaculum, a show.
intro.cn: spectacular 来自拉丁语 spectare（观看），经 spectaculum（表演）而来。

items.en: Spectare meant to look at or watch.
items.cn: spectare 意为观看、注视。

items.en: Spectaculum meant a show or a sight.
items.cn: spectaculum 意为表演或景象。

items.en: Spectacular entered English meaning of a show.
items.cn: spectacular 以「表演的」之义进入英语。

items.en: It spread to views and natural scenery.
items.cn: 它扩展到景色和自然风光。

items.en: It came to describe surprising success or failure.
items.cn: 它逐渐用来形容惊人的成功或失败。

note.en: Spectacular is compared with look-alike words and words for magnificence.
note.cn: 把 spectacular 与形近词以及表示壮丽的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Spectacular is a sight that makes the crowd look up and forget itself.
normalIntro.cn: spectacular 是让人群抬头、忘掉自己的景象。

normal.en: Fireworks burst over the river in a spectacular display.
normal.cn: 烟花在河面上空绽放，景象十分壮观。

normal.en: The team made a spectacular comeback.
normal.cn: 这支队伍实现了惊人的逆转。

normal.en: The show ended with a spectacular finale.
normal.cn: 演出以精彩的终场结束。

normal.en: The mountain road offers a spectacular view.
normal.cn: 山路上有壮观的景色。

normal.en: Her first novel was a spectacular success.
normal.cn: 她的第一部小说获得了惊人的成功。

abstract.en: A spectacle is a sight that charges admission to the heart.
abstract.cn: 奇观是向心脏收费的景象。

abstract.en: What is spectacular soon becomes ordinary.
abstract.cn: 壮观的景象，很快就会变得平常。

abstract.en: The greatest shows leave silence behind.
abstract.cn: 最盛大的演出，留下的是寂静。

examples.en: Fireworks burst over the river in a spectacular display.
examples.cn: 烟花在河面上空绽放，景象十分壮观。

examples.en: The team made a spectacular comeback.
examples.cn: 这支队伍实现了惊人的逆转。

examples.en: The show ended with a spectacular finale.
examples.cn: 演出以精彩的终场结束。

dict_mnemonic.text: spectacular 源自拉丁语 spectare（观看），表示「壮观的、惊人的」；副词 spectacularly 是「壮观地」，名词 spectacle 是「景象、奇观」，spectator 是「观众」，同根词还有 inspect、respect。

root: 来自拉丁语 spectare（观看），经 spectaculum（表演、景象）进入英语，核心义为值得一看的、景象壮观的，后引申为惊人的。

sensesIntro.en: Spectacular means impressive to see, surprisingly great, or brilliantly performed.
sensesIntro.cn: spectacular 指看上去壮观、大得出人意料，或表演精彩。

core.en: A sight that holds every eye.
core.cn: 抓住所有目光的景象。

branches.en: Fire fills the sky above a river.
branches.cn: 火光充满河面上方的天空。

branches.en: A losing team turns the game around.
branches.cn: 落后的队伍扭转了比赛。

branches.en: The curtain falls on a room full of applause.
branches.cn: 帷幕在满场掌声中落下。

branches.en: A landscape and a stage can both astonish.
branches.cn: 风景与舞台都能令人惊叹。

branches.en: A great result and a great show share one word.
branches.cn: 惊人的成绩与精彩的演出共用一个词。

intro.en: Spectacular connects to the Latin family of watching.
intro.cn: spectacular 与拉丁语中表示观看的词族相连。

latinIntro.en: The roots are spectare, to watch, and spectaculum, a show.
latinIntro.cn: 其词根是 spectare（观看）和 spectaculum（表演）。

items.example: Fireworks burst over the river in a spectacular display.
items.exampleCN: 烟花在河面上空绽放，景象十分壮观。

items.example: The storm was a wild spectacle.
items.exampleCN: 那场风暴是狂野的奇观。

items.example: They came to spectate, not to play.
items.exampleCN: 他们是来看比赛的，不是来打的。

definition_en: happening quickly, moving fast, or able to act without delay
core_image: 一只雨燕贴着桥面掠过水面
scene: 警方的反应既迅速又果断。 The police response was swift and firm.
sceneCN: 这里 swift 是「迅速的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：警方的反应既迅速又果断。

senses.title: Happening quickly
senses.definition: happening or done very quickly
senses.definitionCN: 发生或完成得很快
senses.example: The police response was swift and firm.
senses.exampleCN: 警方的反应既迅速又果断。
senses.why: This is the general sense of speed.
senses.whyCN: 这是一般的速度义项。

senses.title: Quick to act
senses.definition: able to move or act fast
senses.definitionCN: 能够快速移动或行动
senses.example: She was swift to catch the ball.
senses.exampleCN: 她敏捷地接住了球。
senses.why: Speed becomes a personal ability.
senses.whyCN: 速度变成个人能力。

senses.title: A fast bird
senses.definition: a small bird known for fast flight
senses.definitionCN: 以飞行快速著称的小鸟
senses.example: A swift circled above the tower.
senses.exampleCN: 一只雨燕在塔上方盘旋。
senses.why: The adjective also names the fast bird.
senses.whyCN: 形容词也用来称这种快鸟。

intro.en: Swift is an old Germanic word for moving quickly.
intro.cn: swift 是表示快速移动的古老日耳曼词。

items.en: Swiftaz meant moving quickly.
items.cn: swiftaz 意为快速移动的。

items.en: Swift meant quick.
items.cn: swift 意为快的。

items.en: Swift meant speedy or ready.
items.cn: swift 意为迅速的或敏捷的。

items.en: Swift described quick action.
items.cn: swift 描述迅速的行动。

items.en: Swift also named the fast bird.
items.cn: swift 也用来称这种快鸟。

note.en: Swift is compared with look-alike words and with words for speed.
note.cn: 把 swift 与形近词以及表示快速的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Swift is speed with a clean, sure line.
normalIntro.cn: swift 是干净利落的速度。

normal.en: The police response was swift and firm.
normal.cn: 警方的反应既迅速又果断。

normal.en: She was swift to catch the ball.
normal.cn: 她敏捷地接住了球。

normal.en: A swift circled above the tower.
normal.cn: 一只雨燕在塔上方盘旋。

normal.en: The court promised swift justice.
normal.cn: 法院承诺迅速审判。

normal.en: He took swift action after the alarm.
normal.cn: 警报响后他迅速采取行动。

abstract.en: Swift is speed without hesitation.
abstract.cn: swift 是毫不犹豫的速度。

abstract.en: The bird and the decision share one word.
abstract.cn: 飞鸟与决定共用一个词。

abstract.en: What is swift leaves little time for doubt.
abstract.cn: 迅速之物几乎不给怀疑留时间。

examples.en: The police response was swift and firm.
examples.cn: 警方的反应既迅速又果断。

examples.en: She was swift to catch the ball.
examples.cn: 她敏捷地接住了球。

examples.en: A swift circled above the tower.
examples.cn: 一只雨燕在塔上方盘旋。
