root: 来自古英语 swift（快的），源于日耳曼语 swiftaz。

sensesIntro.en: Swift means quick, able to act fast, or the fast-flying bird.
sensesIntro.cn: swift 表示迅速、敏捷，或指雨燕。

core.en: Motion with no wasted time.
core.cn: 没有浪费时间的运动。

branches.en: The police response was swift and firm.
branches.cn: 警方的反应既迅速又果断。

branches.en: The court promised swift justice.
branches.cn: 法院承诺迅速审判。

branches.en: She was swift to catch the ball.
branches.cn: 她敏捷地接住了球。

branches.en: A swift circled above the tower.
branches.cn: 一只雨燕在塔上方盘旋。

branches.en: A quick bird and a quick decision both swerve little.
branches.cn: 快鸟与快决定都少有偏移。

intro.en: Swift forms swifter, swiftest and the adverb swiftly.
intro.cn: swift 构成比较级、最高级以及副词 swiftly。

latinIntro.en: Swift is Germanic; Latin velox, fast, gives velocity.
latinIntro.cn: swift 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 velox（快）衍生出 velocity。

latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 rapidus 意为迅速的。

definition_zh: 排水；流干；排水沟；下水道；耗尽；流失
definition_en: to make liquid flow away, or a pipe or channel that carries waste water away
core_image: 水池底部的旋涡，把所有水都吸下去
scene: 厨房水槽堵了，脏水漫过池沿，地面一片湿滑。 He had to drain the sink before fixing the pipe.
sceneCN: 这里 drain 是「把水排掉」（第 1 个义项）；句意是他得先把水槽里的水排掉才能修管道。

pos.zh: 名词：排水沟；下水道；消耗

derivatives.zh: 由 drain 加名词后缀 -age 构成，义为「排水系统；排水」
由 drain 加 pipe 复合而成，义为「排水管」
由 drain 加 -ed 构成，义为「筋疲力尽的」

senses.title: To make liquid flow away
senses.definition: to remove water or another liquid from something by letting it flow out
senses.definitionCN: 让水或其他液体流出去，从而把它从某物中清除
senses.example: Drain the rice and leave it to cool.
senses.exampleCN: 把米沥干，放凉。
senses.why: The word descends from a Germanic root meaning to make dry, so its first job is simply to take liquid away.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自表示「使干」的日耳曼词根，所以它最初的工作就是把液体带走。

senses.title: To flow away gradually
senses.definition: to flow out slowly until little or nothing is left
senses.definitionCN: 慢慢流出去，直到所剩无几
senses.example: The flood water drained away overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水一夜之间退去了。
senses.why: When the object is the liquid itself rather than a container, the same action becomes an intransitive flowing away.
senses.whyCN: 当对象是液体本身而不是容器时，同一个动作就变成不及物的「流走」。

senses.title: A channel that carries waste water
senses.definition: a pipe or open channel that carries away waste water or rainwater
senses.definitionCN: 把污水或雨水送走的管道或明沟
senses.example: Leaves blocked the drain outside the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 落叶堵住了门外的排水沟。
senses.why: The thing that performs the draining takes the action's name, so the channel itself is called a drain.
senses.whyCN: 执行「排」这个动作的装置沿用了动作的名称，于是排水沟本身也叫 drain。

senses.title: To use up strength or money
senses.definition: to take away someone's energy, money, or resources until little is left
senses.definitionCN: 把某人的精力、金钱或资源抽走，直到所剩无几
senses.example: The long illness drained the family's savings.
senses.exampleCN: 这场漫长的病耗尽了家里的积蓄。
senses.why: Energy and money behave like liquid in this metaphor: they can be drawn out until the container is empty.
senses.whyCN: 在这个比喻里，精力与金钱就像液体，可以被抽走，直到容器见底。

senses.title: A steady loss of something valuable
senses.definition: a continuous loss of people, skills, or money from a place or system
senses.definitionCN: 人员、技能或资金从一个地方或体系中持续流失
senses.example: The countryside suffers from a steady drain of young workers.
senses.exampleCN: 乡村正承受年轻劳动力持续外流的压力。
senses.why: If draining empties a container drop by drop, the noun also names that slow emptying of a whole region.
senses.whyCN: 如果排水是一滴一滴把容器放空，那么这个名词也指一整个地区被慢慢抽空的过程。

intro.en: Drain comes from Old English drehnian, to strain or draw off liquid, and its family is Germanic.
intro.cn: drain 来自古英语 drehnian，意为「滤出、抽走液体」，其词族属日耳曼语。

items.en: A root meaning to make dry or to strain lies behind the English word; the exact shape is reconstructed.
items.cn: 英语这个词背后有一个表示「使干、过滤」的词根，其确切形态是重构出来的。

items.en: Drehnian meant to strain liquid off or to draw it away.
items.cn: drehnian 意为把液体滤出或抽走。

items.en: The verb settled as drayne and extended from kitchens to fields and mines.
items.cn: 动词固定为 drayne，并从厨房扩展到田地与矿井。

items.en: The noun appeared for the channel that carries water away; the earliest examples are roughly dated.
items.cn: 名词出现，指把水送走的沟渠；最早用例的年代只能大致推定。

items.en: The liquid image spread to energy, savings, and the loss of skilled people from a region.
items.cn: 液体的意象扩展到精力、积蓄，以及一个地区技术人才的外流。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the stem; the near-meaning group separates removing liquid from using it up.
note.cn: 形近组共享词干；近义组把「排出液体」与「耗光」分开。

entries.definition: The system or process by which water is carried away.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「排水；排水系统」，由 drain 加 -age 构成。

entries.definition: A pipe that carries waste water away from a building.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「排水管」，由 drain 与 pipe 复合。

entries.definition: Extremely tired, as if emptied of energy.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「筋疲力尽的」，字面是「被抽空了」。

entries.definition: To remove everything from a container, not only liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「清空」，对象不限于液体。

entries.definition: To use something up completely, especially resources or energy.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「耗尽」，多用于资源与精力。

entries.definition: An underground pipe for waste water and sewage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「下水道」，规模比 drain 更大、更专门。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the liquid image from the sink to the region losing its workers.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着液体的意象，从水槽一路走到人才外流的地区。

normal.en: Drain and dry share a meaning, so the word is about removing wetness.
normal.cn: drain 与 dry 意义相通，这个词的核心就是「去湿」。

normal.en: A drain is simply the thing that does the draining.
normal.cn: drain 这个装置，就是执行「排」这个动作的东西。

normal.en: Energy drains like water, which is why tired people feel drained.
normal.cn: 精力像水一样流走，所以累坏的人会觉得被抽空了。

normal.en: Brain drain means the cleverest people flow out of a country.
normal.cn: brain drain 指最聪明的人像水一样流出国外。

normal.en: A drain on resources is a slow leak you keep paying for.
normal.cn: a drain on resources 就是一处你不断为之付钱的慢性漏水。

abstract.en: Picture a whirlpool above a plug hole.
abstract.cn: 想象排水口上方转起的旋涡。

abstract.en: Picture a bathtub slowly emptying after the plug is pulled.
abstract.cn: 想象拔掉塞子后浴缸慢慢见底。

abstract.en: Picture an hourglass whose sand will not stop falling.
abstract.cn: 想象一只沙漏，沙子怎么也停不下来。

examples.en: Please drain the pasta before you add the sauce.
examples.cn: 加酱之前请先把面里的水沥干。

examples.en: The drain in the yard is blocked again.
examples.cn: 院子里的排水沟又堵了。

examples.en: Endless paperwork drained her energy.
examples.cn: 没完没了的文书工作耗尽了她的精力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拽阴」——把水往阴沟里拽，drain 就是「排水、流走」。

root: 来自古英语 drehnian（滤出、抽走液体），属日耳曼语词族，与表示「使干」的词根相关。由「排掉液体」引申为「流走」、「排水沟」，再由液体的流失引申为精力、金钱的耗尽与人才外流。

sensesIntro.en: A single image of water leaving a container grows into pipes, exhaustion, and regional loss.
sensesIntro.cn: 「水离开容器」这一个画面，长出了管道、疲惫与地区性流失。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whirlpool pulling every drop down a plug hole.
core.cn: 核心意象：旋涡把每一滴水都吸进排水口。

branches.en: WATER: the verb works both on the container and on the liquid itself.
branches.cn: 水线：这个动词既能作用在容器上，也能作用在液体本身上，即第一、二个义项。

branches.en: THE PIPE: the device that drains takes the action's name.
branches.cn: 管道线：执行排水动作的装置沿用了动作之名，即第三个义项。

branches.en: THE BODY: strength and money can be poured out like water.
branches.cn: 身体线：体力与金钱可以像水一样被倒空，即第四个义项。

branches.en: THE REGION: a place slowly empties of its skilled people.
branches.cn: 地区线：一个地方慢慢被抽走它的技术人才，即第五个义项。

branches.en: Draining a sink and draining a person share the same emptying motion.
branches.cn: 把水槽排空与把人耗空，共享同一个「倒空」的动作。

intro.en: Drain is a whole Germanic verb that also takes English endings and compounds.
intro.cn: drain 是完整的日耳曼语动词，同时能接英语词尾并参与复合。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved; drainage uses a French-derived suffix that itself goes back to Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词本身没有拉丁成分；drainage 用的 -age 后缀经法语转来，再往上才是拉丁语。

items.example: The old verb is the source of drain.
items.exampleCN: 这个古动词是 drain 的来源。

items.example: Pulling the plug lets the water drain.

derivatives.zh: 由 drain 加 -age 构成，义为「排水；排水系统」
由 drain 与 pipe 复合，义为「排水管」

definition_en: a situation in which there is not enough of something that is needed
core_image: 空荡荡的货架，只剩下几张写着「售罄」的纸牌
scene: 炎热夏天城市面临缺水。 The city faces a water shortage in hot summers.
sceneCN: 这里 shortage 是「短缺」（第 1 个义项）；句意：炎热夏天城市面临缺水。

senses.title: Not enough supply
senses.definition: a lack of something needed
senses.definitionCN: 缺少某种需要的东西
senses.example: The city faces a water shortage in hot summers.
senses.exampleCN: 炎热夏天城市面临缺水。
senses.why: This is the general modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是常见的现代义项。

senses.title: Empty shelves
senses.definition: a lack of goods in shops
senses.definitionCN: 商店里商品不足
senses.example: There is a shortage of fresh milk.
senses.exampleCN: 鲜奶缺货。
senses.why: The general lack becomes a retail problem.
senses.whyCN: 普遍短缺成为零售问题。

senses.title: Not enough staff
senses.definition: a lack of workers
senses.definitionCN: 工作人员不足
senses.example: The hospital has a nurse shortage.
senses.exampleCN: 医院缺少护士。
senses.why: People can be short as well as goods.
senses.whyCN: 人和货物都可能短缺。

intro.en: Shortage joins short with the noun ending -age.
intro.cn: shortage 由 short 加名词后缀 -age 构成。

items.en: Sceort meant short or lacking.
items.cn: sceort 意为短的或不足的。

items.en: Short of meant not having enough.
items.cn: short of 意为没有足够的。

items.en: Shortage named a lack of goods.
items.cn: shortage 指商品短缺。

items.en: Shortage extended to workers and services.
items.cn: shortage 扩展到人手与服务。

items.en: Shortage became common in news and policy.
items.cn: shortage 在新闻与政策中变得常见。

note.en: Shortage is compared with similar-looking words and with words for lack.
note.cn: 把 shortage 与形近词以及表示缺乏的词作比较。

entries.definition: a small list of chosen candidates
the state of not having something
the amount by which something is too small

normalIntro.en: A shortage is an empty space where something should be.
normalIntro.cn: shortage 是本该有东西的地方空了出来。

normal.en: There is a water shortage.
normal.cn: 出现了缺水。

normal.en: The shop has a bread shortage.
normal.cn: 这家店面包缺货。

normal.en: The hospital faces a staff shortage.
normal.cn: 医院面临人手短缺。

normal.en: Housing shortages worried the city.
normal.cn: 住房短缺让城市担忧。

normal.en: A shortage of rain hurt the crops.
normal.cn: 雨水不足损害了庄稼。

abstract.en: Shortage is the shadow of demand.
abstract.cn: 短缺是需求的影子。

abstract.en: An empty shelf teaches the price of plenty.
abstract.cn: 空货架让人懂得充裕的代价。

abstract.en: Some shortages are made by fear, not by nature.
abstract.cn: 有些短缺源于恐惧而非自然。

examples.en: The city faces a water shortage in hot summers.
examples.cn: 炎热夏天城市面临缺水。

examples.en: There is a shortage of fresh milk.
examples.cn: 鲜奶缺货。

examples.en: The hospital has a nurse shortage.
examples.cn: 医院缺少护士。

dict_mnemonic.text: shortage 就是 short 加 -age：东西变短了、不够了，就形成「短缺」这种状态。

root: 由 short（不足）加 -age（状态）构成，核心义「供给不足的状态」。

sensesIntro.en: Shortage means not enough supply, empty shelves, or not enough staff.
sensesIntro.cn: shortage 意为短缺、缺货或缺员。

core.en: The gap between supply and need.
core.cn: 供给与需求之间的缺口。

branches.en: Water runs low in summer.
branches.cn: 夏天水变少了。

branches.en: Milk disappears from the shelf.
branches.cn: 牛奶从货架上消失。

branches.en: Nurses are too few.
branches.cn: 护士人数太少。

branches.en: A general lack appears as empty stock.
branches.cn: 普遍短缺表现为空库存。

branches.en: Goods and workers can both run out.
branches.cn: 货物与工人都会耗尽。

intro.en: Shortage forms a small family of lack words.
intro.cn: shortage 形成一个表示缺乏的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Shortage is Germanic plus the French noun ending -age.
latinIntro.cn: shortage 由日耳曼语词根加法语名词后缀 -age 构成。

items.example: A fuel shortage stopped the trucks.
items.exampleCN: 燃料短缺让卡车停了下来。

items.example: Food shortages spread across the region.
items.exampleCN: 粮食短缺蔓延整个地区。

items.example: The island is short-supplied in winter.
The warehouse aims to be shortage-free.

definition_en: to show approval by clapping the hands, or to praise a person, action, or idea
core_image: 双手拍在一起的声音：用掌声把喜欢和赞成表达出来
scene: 演出结束，观众纷纷起身。 The audience stood up to applaud the pianist after her final piece.
sceneCN: 这里 applaud 是「鼓掌；喝彩」（第 1 个义项：拍手表示赞赏）；句意为「钢琴家弹完最后一曲后，观众起身为她鼓掌」。这个词既可以指真实的拍手动作，也可以引申为口头或态度上的称赞。

pos.zh: 称赞；赞许（某人、某行为或某决定）

derivatives.zh: applaud 加名词后缀 -se 构成，义为「鼓掌；掌声；喝彩」
applaud 加施动者后缀 -er 构成，义为「鼓掌者；称赞者」
applaud 加形容词后缀 -able 的少见变体，义为「值得称赞的」，更常用 plausible 之外的形式 praiseworthy 表达

senses.title: To clap the hands to show enjoyment
senses.definition: to hit your hands together repeatedly to show that you enjoyed a performance
senses.definitionCN: 反复拍手，表示欣赏演出或表演
senses.example: The audience applauded loudly at the end of the concert.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐会结束时，观众热烈鼓掌。
senses.why: The core image is hands coming together to make sound; the most direct use is the physical clap itself.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是双手相击发出声响；最直接的用法就是拍手这个物理动作本身。

senses.title: To clap to welcome or thank someone
senses.definition: to clap in order to welcome a person onto a stage or to thank them
senses.definitionCN: 以掌声欢迎某人上台，或以掌声表示感谢
senses.example: Please applaud our next speaker as she comes to the stage.
senses.exampleCN: 下一位演讲者上台时，请大家鼓掌欢迎。
senses.why: The clap is directed at a person as a social gesture, extending the physical action to a ritual of welcome or thanks.
senses.whyCN: 掌声指向某个人，成为一种社交姿态；物理动作延伸为欢迎或致谢的仪式。

senses.title: To praise a performance or achievement publicly
senses.definition: to publicly praise a performance, work, or achievement, especially in the media
senses.definitionCN: 公开称赞演出、作品或成就，尤见于媒体报道
senses.example: Critics applauded the young director's first film.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家们盛赞这位年轻导演的首部电影。
senses.why: Approval that once needed clapping can now be expressed in words; the sound of praise replaces the sound of hands.
senses.whyCN: 原本需要鼓掌表达的赞许，如今可以用言语表达；赞许之声取代了拍手之声。

senses.title: To express strong approval of a decision or action
senses.definition: to say or show that you strongly approve of a decision, action, or idea
senses.definitionCN: 表示强烈赞成某个决定、行为或想法
senses.example: Environmental groups applauded the government's new policy.
senses.exampleCN: 环保团体对政府的新政策表示赞许。
senses.why: When the object is abstract, applaud no longer means clapping but standing behind something with approval.
senses.whyCN: 当宾语是抽象事物时，applaud 不再指拍手，而是表示对某事的认同与支持。

senses.title: To praise someone for a specific quality or effort
senses.titleCN: 因品质或努力而称赞某人
senses.definition: to praise a person for a particular quality, effort, or courage, often with for
senses.definitionCN: 常与 for 连用，因某种品质、努力或勇气而称赞某人
senses.example: Teachers applauded the students for their honesty.
senses.exampleCN: 老师们称赞学生诚实。
senses.why: The pattern applaud sb for sth treats praise as a reward given to a person, like applause given to a performer.
senses.whyCN: applaud sb for sth 结构把称赞看作给一个人的奖励，正如把掌声献给表演者。

senses.title: To be worthy of praise
senses.definition: to deserve praise, used in passive or descriptive sentences about actions or qualities
senses.definitionCN: 用于被动或描述性句子，指行为或品质值得称赞
senses.example: His courage in speaking up deserves to be applauded.
senses.exampleCN: 他敢于发声的勇气值得称道。
senses.why: Approval as a reward can be described as owed; something so good that it should receive the clap of praise.
senses.whyCN: 赞许作为一种奖励，可被描述为「应得的」；好到理应收获掌声的赞美。

intro.en: Applaud comes from Latin via Italian, built on a root meaning to clap or strike together.
intro.cn: applaud 经意大利语进入英语，词根义为「拍击；相击而响」。

items.en: Latin applaudere, from ad- (toward) + plaudere (to clap, strike), meaning to clap in approval.
items.cn: 拉丁语 applaudere，由 ad-（朝向）+ plaudere（拍击）构成，义为「拍手表示赞成」。

items.en: The compound verb spread in Late Latin and gave related forms like plausus, a clapping or a sound of approval.
items.cn: 这一复合动词在晚期拉丁语中通行，并派生出 plausus（拍打声；赞许声）等相关形式。

items.en: The word passed into Italian as applaudire before entering English.
items.cn: 该词先进入意大利语，作 applaudire，随后进入英语。

items.en: Applaud is first recorded in English in the late 1500s, at first meaning to clap or express approval.
items.cn: applaud 于十六世纪末在英语中首次见于记载，最初义为拍手或表示赞许。

items.en: The sense broadened from literal clapping to public and figurative praise of ideas, decisions, and people.
items.cn: 词义从字面鼓掌扩展为对想法、决定和人物的公开或比喻性称赞。

note.en: These words share spelling or meaning patterns with applaud, but differ in force or usage.
note.cn: 以下词语与 applaud 在拼写或词义上相关，但在语气或用法上有区别。

entries.definitionCN: 同根名词，指鼓掌的声音；掌声

entries.definition: a round fruit; only looks similar at the start of the word
entries.definitionCN: 一种水果；仅词首拼写相近，与 applaud 词源无关

entries.definition: to make a formal request; shares the prefix ap- but has a different root
entries.definitionCN: 申请；应用；与前缀 ap- 相同但词根不同，只是拼写相近

entries.definition: seeming reasonable; from the same Latin root plaudere
entries.definitionCN: 看似有理的；与 applaud 同源于拉丁语 plaudere，原义与掌声相关

entries.definition: to hit the hands together; plainer and more physical than applaud
entries.definitionCN: 拍手；比 applaud 更口语、更侧重动作本身

entries.definition: to express strong approval in words; general-purpose praise
entries.definitionCN: 称赞；用言语表达赞许，泛用性最强

entries.definition: to shout in support or joy; louder and more emotional than clapping
entries.definitionCN: 欢呼；以喊叫表示支持或高兴，比鼓掌情绪更外放
嘉奖；正式或官方的称赞，语气庄重

normalIntro.en: Build the word from its Latin parts and sound family.
normalIntro.cn: 从拉丁语部件和声音家族来搭建这个词。

normal.en: ap- + plaud: the prefix ap- (toward) plus the root plaud (clap) makes 'clap toward someone'.
normal.cn: ap-（朝向）+ plaud（拍击）＝「朝某人拍手」，即鼓掌赞许。

normal.en: applause is the noun twin: you applaud, and the result is applause.
normal.cn: applause 是名词孪生兄弟：你 applaud（鼓掌），产生的就是 applause（掌声）。

normal.en: plausible shares the root plaud: what gets applause sounds plausible.
normal.cn: plausible 与 applaud 同根：能赢得掌声的说法，听起来就显得可信。

normal.en: Sound link: 'a-PLOD' — picture the audience plodding hands together again and again.
normal.cn: 读音联想「厄-普洛德」：想象观众双手像踏步一样一下一下拍个不停。

normal.en: Opposite pair: applaud to approve, boo to reject — a theatre needs both.
normal.cn: 对比记忆：applaud 表示赞成，boo 表示喝倒彩——剧院里两者都有。

abstract.en: Picture two hands meeting like friends shaking hands: approval made audible.
abstract.cn: 想象双手相会如友人握手：赞许被变成了声音。

abstract.en: Applaud is approval you can hear; praise is approval you can read.
abstract.cn: applaud 是听得见的赞许，praise 是读得到的赞许。

abstract.en: Think of a switch that turns liking into sound: press it, and the room claps.
abstract.cn: 把它想成把「喜欢」转换成声音的开关：一按，满堂掌声。

examples.en: The whole audience applauded when the singer came on stage.
examples.cn: 歌手登台时，全场观众鼓掌。

examples.en: We applaud her decision to continue her studies.
examples.cn: 我们赞许她继续深造的决定。

examples.en: His speech was warmly applauded by the teachers.
examples.cn: 他的演讲赢得老师们热烈的掌声。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿婆劳的」——阿婆看得劳累的演出结束时也劳着双手鼓掌，掌声不断，声似「阿婆劳的」。

root: 源自拉丁语 applaudere：前缀 ad-（朝向）+ 词根 plaudere（拍击；拍手作响）。词根 plaud- 还见于 applause（掌声）与 plausible（貌似有理的，原义「值得掌声的」）。拉丁词形确凿，无存疑。

sensesIntro.en: From the physical clap, the word grows into welcoming, praising, and approving.
sensesIntro.cn: 词义从「拍手」这一物理动作出发，延伸为欢迎、称赞与认同。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands striking together to turn approval into sound
core.cn: 核心意象：双手相击，把赞许变成听得见的声音

branches.en: The literal clap: enjoying a show or greeting a person with sound.
branches.cn: 字面拍手：为演出喝彩，或以掌声欢迎某人。

branches.en: Praise in words replaces clapping for works and performances.
branches.cn: 对作品与演出，言语称赞取代了拍手。

branches.en: Approval extends to decisions, policies, and ideas.
branches.cn: 赞许扩展到决定、政策与想法。

branches.en: Praise becomes personal: applauding someone for a quality.
branches.cn: 称赞变得具体：因某种品质而称赞某人。

branches.en: Approval turns into a reward that good actions deserve.
branches.cn: 赞许变成好行为应得的奖励。

intro.en: Applaud is built from a Latin prefix and a sound-related root, with a small word family.
intro.cn: applaud 由拉丁语前缀和与声音相关的词根构成，并有一个不大的词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root plaud- also appears in other English and Latin words about striking and approval.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 plaud- 还出现在其他与拍击、赞许相关的英语及拉丁语词中。

items.example: In applaud, the clap is directed toward the performer.
items.exampleCN: 在 applaud 中，拍击朝向表演者。

items.example: Plaudere is the Latin verb behind applaud.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁动词 plaudere 是 applaud 的来源。

items.meaningCN: 拉丁语动词不定式词尾
items.example: Plaudere shows the raw dictionary form of the verb.
items.exampleCN: plaudere 展示该动词的原始词形。

items.meaningCN: 掌声；以声音表示的赞许
items.exampleCN: 雷鸣般的掌声响彻大厅。

items.meaning: seeming worthy of applause, hence believable
items.meaningCN: 貌似可信的；原义「值得掌声的」

items.example: The root also gave explosion, a sound of bursting.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根还派生出 explosion（爆炸），指爆裂之声。

items.example: Every applauder added to the noise.
items.exampleCN: 每位鼓掌者都让声响更大。

items.meaning: the act of clapping in progress
items.example: The applauding crowd would not stop.
items.exampleCN: 鼓掌的人群久久不肯停下。

latinEntries.meaning: a clapping; a sound of approval

definition_en: the place that someone or something is travelling to
core_image: 长途车窗外的路牌，一个地名后面跟着一支箭头
scene: 大巴在夜里开了很久，司机终于报出那个熟悉的地名。 After ten hours on the road, they reached their destination.
sceneCN: 这里 destination 指「目的地」（第 1 个义项：旅程要去的地方）；句意是在路上走了十个小时后，他们到达了目的地。

senses.title: The place you are going to
senses.definition: the place that a person or vehicle is travelling toward
senses.definitionCN: 人或车辆正在前往的那个地方
senses.example: After ten hours on the road, they reached their destination.
senses.exampleCN: 在路上走了十个小时后，他们到达了目的地。
senses.why: A journey needs one fixed point for every turn to point at.
senses.whyCN: 一段旅程需要一个固定的点，让每一次转弯都有所指。

senses.title: The end of the line
senses.definition: the final stop on a route or transport service
senses.definitionCN: 某条路线或交通线路的最后一站
senses.example: This train's destination is the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 这趟列车的终点是海边。
senses.why: Tracks end somewhere, and the map must name that end.
senses.whyCN: 轨道总在某处结束，地图必须给那个结束命名。

senses.title: A place people travel to
senses.definition: a place that many people choose to visit for pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 许多人为了游玩而选择前往的地方
senses.example: The old port is now a favourite destination for divers.
senses.exampleCN: 这座旧港口如今是潜水者喜爱的去处。
senses.why: When enough people aim at one place, the place becomes the word.
senses.whyCN: 当足够多的人朝同一个地方去，那个地方就成了这个词本身。

intro.en: Destination comes from Latin destinare, to fix or make firm, built on de- and stare, to stand, so a destination is a point fixed to stand at.
intro.cn: destination 来自拉丁语 destinare（固定、定下），由 de- 与 stare（站立）构成，目的地就是一个被定住要站到的点。

items.en: Stare meant to stand, and destinare meant to make something stand firm.
items.cn: stare 指站立，destinare 指使某物稳稳立住。

items.en: It was used for fixing a purpose, a date or a place in advance.
items.cn: 它用于事先定下目的、日期或地点。

items.en: Destinatio named the act of fixing, and later the fixed point.
items.cn: destinatio 指固定的动作，后来指被固定的那个点。

items.en: French destination carried the travel sense into English.
items.cn: 法语 destination 把旅行的意思带进了英语。

items.en: Tourism turned the word into a label for places worth visiting.
items.cn: 旅游业又把这个词变成值得一去的那些地方的标签。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the destin- stem of fate and fixing, and the meaning group all name an end point.
note.cn: 形近组共用 destin- 这个表示命运与固定的词干，近义组则都指一个终点。

entries.definition: what is fated to happen to someone
entries.definitionCN: 某人命中注定要遇到的事

entries.definition: certain to happen or to go somewhere
entries.definitionCN: 注定发生或注定前往的

entries.definition: to set aside for a purpose
the result you are trying to reach
the last stop of a bus or train line
entries.definitionCN: 公交线或铁路的终点站

entries.definition: an aim that is chosen in advance

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a road sign at night and end with a harbour full of divers.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从夜里的一块路牌开始，落到一个挤满潜水者的港口。

normal.en: A destination is a point the map has agreed to stand still for.
normal.cn: 目的地就是地图答应站着不动的那一点。

normal.en: Destinare meant to fix, so the place is fixed before you leave.
normal.cn: destinare 本是固定，所以地方在你出发前就定好了。

normal.en: A train has a destination; a walk may only have a direction.
normal.cn: 列车有目的地，散步有时只有方向。

normal.en: When a place draws crowds, it becomes a destination by itself.
normal.cn: 一个地方招来人群，它自己就成了目的地。

normal.en: The word shares a stem with destiny, which is a destination in time.
normal.cn: 这个词与 destiny 同根，命运不过是时间里的目的地。

abstract.en: Picture a white arrow on a dark blue sign.
abstract.cn: 想象深蓝色路牌上的一支白色箭头。

abstract.en: Picture a bus door opening onto a lit platform at midnight.
abstract.cn: 想象午夜车门打开，外面是一处亮着灯的站台。

abstract.en: Picture a suitcase set down at the end of a long lane.
abstract.cn: 想象一只箱子被放在一条长巷的尽头。

examples.en: After ten hours on the road, they reached their destination.
examples.cn: 在路上走了十个小时后，他们到达了目的地。

examples.en: This train's destination is the coast.
examples.cn: 这趟列车的终点是海边。

examples.en: The old port is now a favourite destination for divers.
examples.cn: 这座旧港口如今是潜水者喜爱的去处。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 destination 记成「地斯提内神」：de 向下，st 像「站」，定住站下的那个点，就是目的地。

root: 来自拉丁语 destinare（固定、定下），由 de- 与 stare（站立）构成，名词 destinatio 指固定的动作与固定的点，经法语进入英语。本义是被定下来要到达的地方，后来指交通线路的终点，也指人们专程前往的旅游地。

sensesIntro.en: From the point a journey aims at, to the end of a line, to a place that draws travellers by itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 从旅程所指向的点，到一条线路的尽头，再到本身就能招来旅人的地方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fixed point on a map with an arrow pointing to it.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上一个被箭头指着的固定点。

branches.en: The first sense is the point a traveller keeps aiming at.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是旅人一直对准的那个点。

branches.en: The second sense is where the rails simply stop.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是铁轨干脆停下的地方。

branches.en: The third sense is a point that attracts many journeys at once.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是同时吸引许多旅程的一个点。

branches.en: A personal aim and a timetable's last stop share the same arrow.
branches.cn: 个人的目标与时刻表的最后一站，共用同一支箭头。

branches.en: Enough private journeys turn a place into a public destination.
branches.cn: 足够多的私人旅程，会把一个地方变成公共的去处。

intro.en: Destination belongs to a family about fixing a point, which also grows the words for fate.
intro.cn: destination 属于一族表示「定下一个点」的词，这一族还长出了表示命运的词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin stare, to stand, and de- makes the standing firm and settled.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是拉丁语 stare（站立），前缀 de- 让这站立变得稳固、确定。

items.example: We reached our destination at dusk.
items.exampleCN: 我们在黄昏时到达目的地。
这条线路通往五个目的地。

items.example: They destined the land for a park.
items.exampleCN: 他们把那块地定为公园。

items.example: Chance destines some plans to fail.
items.exampleCN: 偶然让一些计划注定失败。

items.example: They were destined to meet again.

items.meaning: the act of fixing a purpose
items.example: Destining the site took a week.
items.exampleCN: 为这块地定用途花了一周。

items.meaning: what is fixed for a person
items.exampleCN: 他平静地接受了自己的命运。
这场战争把他们的命运连在一起。

definition_en: an aircraft with spinning blades on top that can rise straight up, or to carry someone by such an aircraft
core_image: 头顶巨大的旋翼高速旋转，机身垂直离开地面
scene: 救援直升机把伤员送下山。 A rescue helicopter carried the injured man down the mountain.
sceneCN: 这里 helicopter 是「直升机」（第 1 个义项）；句意：救援直升机把伤员送下山。

senses.title: The aircraft
senses.definition: an aircraft with large spinning blades that can fly straight up
senses.definitionCN: 带大型旋转桨叶、能垂直起飞的飞行器
senses.example: A rescue helicopter carried the injured man down the mountain.
senses.exampleCN: 救援直升机把伤员送下山。
senses.why: This is the machine itself.
senses.whyCN: 这是机器本身。

senses.title: Carry by air
senses.definition: to carry someone or something by helicopter
senses.definitionCN: 用直升机运送人或物
senses.example: They helicoptered food to the flooded village.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用直升机把食物运到被淹的村子。
senses.why: The noun becomes the action of using it.
senses.whyCN: 名词在这里变成了使用它的动作。

intro.en: Helicopter joins Greek helix, spiral, and pteron, wing.
intro.cn: helicopter 由希腊语 helix（螺旋）与 pteron（翼）合成。

items.en: Helix meant a spiral.
items.cn: helix 意为螺旋。

items.en: Pteron meant a wing.
items.cn: pteron 意为翼。

items.en: Hélicoptère combined the two ideas.
items.cn: 法语 hélicoptère 把这两个意思合在一起。

items.en: Helicopter named the new flying machine.
items.cn: helicopter 成为这种新飞行器的名称。

items.en: The word became a verb meaning to fly someone out.
items.cn: 这个词又变成动词，表示用直升机运送。

note.en: Helicopter is compared with words sharing its heli- shape and with other aircraft words.
note.cn: 把 helicopter 与带 heli- 形式的词以及其他飞行器词作比较。

entries.definition: an informal word for a helicopter

normalIntro.en: Helicopter is a spiral wing that lifts straight up.
normalIntro.cn: helicopter 是一片能把机身垂直提起来的螺旋之翼。

normal.en: The helicopter landed on the roof.
normal.cn: 直升机降落在屋顶上。

normal.en: They sent a helicopter to the island.
normal.cn: 他们派了一架直升机去岛上。

normal.en: The pilot flew the helicopter low.
normal.cn: 飞行员把直升机飞得很低。

normal.en: He was helicoptered to the hospital.
normal.cn: 他被直升机送往医院。

normal.en: Helicopter parents watch every step.
normal.cn: 直升机父母盯着孩子的每一步。

abstract.en: A helicopter argues with gravity and wins.
abstract.cn: 直升机与重力争辩，并且赢了。

abstract.en: Its wing goes around so the body can go up.
abstract.cn: 翅膀绕圈，机身才能上升。

abstract.en: Some care hovers like a rotor, never landing.
abstract.cn: 有些关心像旋翼一样悬着，从不落地。

examples.en: A rescue helicopter carried the injured man down the mountain.
examples.cn: 救援直升机把伤员送下山。

examples.en: They helicoptered food to the flooded village.
examples.cn: 他们用直升机把食物运到被淹的村子。

examples.en: The helicopter landed on the roof.
examples.cn: 直升机降落在屋顶上。

dict_mnemonic.text: helicopter 拆开是「螺旋」加「翼」：靠头顶旋转的翼垂直升降；把它当动词用，就是用直升机把人或物运走。

root: 由希腊语 helix（螺旋）与 pteron（翼）经法语 hélicoptère 进入英语；命名依据是它头顶旋转的桨叶，后来也作动词表示用直升机运送。

sensesIntro.en: Helicopter names the rotor aircraft, and then the act of carrying someone by it.
sensesIntro.cn: helicopter 指这种旋翼飞行器，再指用它运送人的动作。

core.en: Blades spinning above a rising body.
core.cn: 旋翼在上升的机身上方飞转。

branches.en: The machine rises straight up.
branches.cn: 机器垂直升起。

branches.en: Supplies fly to a cut-off town.
branches.cn: 物资飞向与外界隔绝的城镇。

branches.en: A pilot hovers above the roof.
branches.cn: 飞行员在屋顶上方悬停。

branches.en: The aircraft becomes a flying ambulance.
branches.cn: 飞行器成了空中救护车。

branches.en: To helicopter someone out is to save time and lives.
branches.cn: 用直升机运人出去，是抢回时间与生命。

intro.en: Helicopter is built from Greek roots and forms verb endings.
intro.cn: helicopter 由希腊词根构成，并加动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The roots are Greek, not Latin: helix and pteron.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词根是希腊语而非拉丁语：helix 与 pteron。

items.exampleCN: 他们用直升机把他运了出去。

items.meaning: the act of flying by helicopter
items.exampleCN: 用直升机运物资成本很高。

items.example: The helipad is on the roof.

items.exampleCN: 直升机机场去年启用了。

definition_en: easily broken or harmed; finely made; needing careful handling
core_image: 薄胎瓷碗托在掌心，手指不敢用力
scene: 她托着那只薄薄的杯子，走路时连呼吸都放轻了。 She carried the thin cup as if it were a delicate shell.
sceneCN: 这里 delicate 指「易碎的」（第 1 个义项：容易碰坏）；句意是她捧着那只薄杯，像捧着一枚易碎的贝壳。

senses.title: Easily broken or hurt
senses.definition: thin or weak enough to be damaged with little force
senses.definitionCN: 薄或弱到稍一用力就会损坏
senses.example: She carried the thin cup as if it were a delicate shell.
senses.exampleCN: 她捧着那只薄杯，像捧着一枚易碎的贝壳。
senses.why: What is lovely is often what breaks first.
senses.whyCN: 好看的东西，往往最先坏。

senses.title: Finely made and pleasing
senses.definition: made with fine skill and a light, careful touch
senses.definitionCN: 以精细手艺和轻巧手法做成
senses.example: The box was carved with a delicate pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 盒子上刻着精致的花纹。
senses.why: Thin lines take longer to cut, and the eye knows it.
senses.whyCN: 细线要花更久去刻，眼睛看得出这份工夫。

senses.title: Needing careful handling
senses.definition: sensitive and easy to upset, of a matter or situation
senses.definitionCN: 指事情或处境敏感，容易被打乱
senses.example: The two countries kept a delicate balance.
senses.exampleCN: 两国之间维持着微妙的平衡。
senses.why: Some things are held together by almost nothing.
senses.whyCN: 有些东西，几乎只靠一点点力气才没有散。

intro.en: Delicate comes from Latin delicatus, which first meant giving pleasure and then finely made.
intro.cn: delicate 来自拉丁语 delicatus，先指令人愉悦，再指做得精细。

items.en: Delicatus described something that delighted the senses.
items.cn: delicatus 形容让感官愉悦的东西。

items.en: Over time it came to mean fine, soft and easily harmed.
items.cn: 后来它又指纤细、柔软、容易受损。

items.en: English used it for fine cloth, food and health.
items.cn: 英语用它形容精细的布、食物和身体。

items.en: The word moved from the body to matters of feeling and politics.
items.cn: 这个词从身体一路挪到情感与政治。

items.en: A delicate matter is one handled with words instead of hands.
items.cn: 如今微妙的事，要用言语而不是手去托。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the deli- opening, and the meaning group moves from breakable to fine to tricky.
note.cn: 形近组共用 deli- 开头，近义组则从易碎走到精细再到棘手。

entries.definition: to give time or effort to a purpose
entries.definitionCN: 把时间或精力献给某个目的

entries.definition: a person sent to act for a group
very thin or made with great skill
not obvious and needing care to notice
entries.definitionCN: 不明显、需要细心才能察觉的

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a thin cup in two hands and end with two countries standing very still.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从双手托着的一只薄杯开始，落到两个一动不动站着的国家。

normal.en: The thinner the cup, the more the hand must listen.
normal.cn: 杯子越薄，手越要会听。

normal.en: Fine lines are slow lines, and the eye pays for them.
normal.cn: 细线都是慢线，眼睛是愿意为此付钱的。

normal.en: A flower proves nothing about strength, only about care.
normal.cn: 花不证明力量，只证明有人肯小心。

normal.en: A delicate balance is not a balance that stays by itself.
normal.cn: 微妙的平衡，不是自己会保持的平衡。

normal.en: Delicacy of taste and delicacy of skin share one skin-thin idea.
normal.cn: 口味的细腻与皮肤的娇嫩，共享同一个「薄」的念头。

abstract.en: Picture a fingertip moving a hair off a page.
abstract.cn: 想象一个指尖把一根头发从纸上捻走。

abstract.en: Picture lace held up against a window.
abstract.cn: 想象一片蕾丝举在窗前。

abstract.en: Picture two glass balls touching and neither breaking.
abstract.cn: 想象两个玻璃球轻轻相触，谁也没碎。

examples.en: She carried the thin cup as if it were a delicate shell.
examples.cn: 她捧着那只薄杯，像捧着一枚易碎的贝壳。

examples.en: The box was carved with a delicate pattern.
examples.cn: 盒子上刻着精致的花纹。

examples.en: The two countries kept a delicate balance.
examples.cn: 两国之间维持着微妙的平衡。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 delicate 记成「得立刻特小心」：薄得一碰就坏，所以得立刻特别小心。

root: 源自拉丁语 delicatus，本义是令人愉悦、讨人喜欢，后来添上纤细、柔软、容易受损的意思。经法语进入英语后，它从布料、食物与身体，一路扩展到情感与局势，于是易碎、精致、微妙三层意思并存。

sensesIntro.en: From a cup that breaks, to work that took great skill, to a balance nobody dares disturb.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一碰就碎的杯子，到极费手艺的活计，再到谁也不敢碰的平衡。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin-walled cup held in two careful hands.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手小心托着一只薄壁杯子。

branches.en: The first sense is thinness that breaks under little force.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是稍一用力就坏的薄。

branches.en: The second sense is thinness used as skill and beauty.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是把薄做成了手艺与美。

branches.en: The third sense is thinness in a situation, where one word can tip it.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是处境的薄，一句话就能打破。

branches.en: What is finely made is also what needs care to keep.
branches.cn: 做得精细的东西，也需要小心才留得住。

branches.en: Both senses praise a thing that cannot be handled roughly.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在说：这东西经不起粗手粗脚。

intro.en: Delicate has nouns and adverbs about fineness, and the noun delicacy carries both taste and care.
intro.cn: delicate 有表示精细的名词与副词，其中 delicacy 既有美味，也有分寸。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is delicatus, pleasing and fine, from deliciae, delight.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 delicatus（悦人而精细），出自 deliciae（愉悦）。

items.meaning: a rare food, or fineness of touch
items.example: The fish is a local delicacy.
The delicateness of the bowl surprised me.
The lake keeps a delicate balance.
items.exampleCN: 这片湖维持着微妙的平衡。

items.example: Money is a delicate issue here.
items.exampleCN: 钱在这里是个敏感话题。

items.example: The tea has a delicate taste.

definition_en: a situation in which people have different opinions, or a failure of two things to match
core_image: 桌子两边各放一摞文件，中间空出一道谁也不过界的缝
scene: 两个人把各自的稿子拉回面前，谁也没有先开口。 There was a sharp disagreement over the budget.
sceneCN: 这里 disagreement 指「分歧」（第 1 个义项：意见不合）；句意是双方在预算上分歧很大。

collocations.phrase: a disagreement between the two sides

senses.title: A clash of opinions
senses.definition: a state in which people hold different views about something
senses.definitionCN: 人们对某事的看法不一样的状态
senses.example: There was a sharp disagreement over the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 双方在预算上分歧很大。
senses.why: Two certainties can stand face to face and both feel right.
senses.whyCN: 两个笃定可以面对面站着，各自都觉得对。

senses.title: An argument that follows
senses.definition: an angry exchange that grows out of different views
senses.definitionCN: 由看法不同发展成的激烈争执
senses.example: A small disagreement grew into a long quarrel.
senses.exampleCN: 一点小分歧变成了一场长吵。
senses.why: The gap between two views becomes a noise before it closes.
senses.whyCN: 两种看法之间的缝，在合上之前先变成了声音。

senses.title: A failure to match
senses.definition: a difference between two things that should be the same
senses.definitionCN: 本应相同的两样东西之间出现的差异
senses.example: There is a disagreement between the two timetables.
senses.exampleCN: 两张时间表对不上。
senses.why: Two lists that should rhyme end on different sounds.
senses.whyCN: 两份本该押韵的清单，收在了不同的音上。

intro.en: Disagreement is disagreement in noun form: dis- plus agreement, which descends from Old French agreer.
intro.cn: disagreement 是动词 disagree 的名词形式：dis- 加 agreement，而 agreement 出自古法语 agreer。

items.en: Gratus meant pleasing and welcome.
items.cn: gratus 指令人愉快、受欢迎的。

items.en: Agreer meant to please or to suit a person.
items.cn: agreer 指使人高兴或合某人的意。

items.en: Agreement named a state of being of one mind.
items.cn: agreement 指意见一致的状态。

items.en: Disagreement named the opposite state, and later a quarrel.
items.cn: disagreement 指相反的状态，后来又指争吵。

items.en: It also covers two records or figures that do not match.
items.cn: 它也可指两份记录或两个数字对不上。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on agree and its negation, while the meaning group names forms of conflict.
note.cn: 形近组建立在 agree 及其否定形式上，近义组则列出几种冲突。

entries.definition: a shared opinion or a formal arrangement
unpleasant or hard to get along with
a serious argument about something important
entries.definitionCN: 围绕重要事情的严肃争论

entries.definition: a long struggle between opposing sides
entries.definitionCN: 对立双方之间的长期冲突

entries.definition: an angry talk in which people disagree
entries.definitionCN: 人们意见不合时的争吵

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a gap on a table to two sets of figures that will not agree.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从桌面上的一道缝，走到两组对不上的数字。

normal.en: Disagreement is the noun of the moment two views part.
normal.cn: disagreement 就是两种看法分开那一刻的名词。

normal.en: A sharp disagreement cuts the air before anyone raises a voice.
normal.cn: 尖锐的分歧，在有人提高嗓门之前就先划开了空气。

normal.en: Two timetables in disagreement cannot both be trusted.
normal.cn: 两张对不上的时间表，不能都信。

normal.en: Resolve the disagreement, and the table feels wider again.
normal.cn: 分歧一解开，桌子好像又宽了。

normal.en: The word keeps the gap visible without naming a winner.
normal.cn: 这个词让那道缝留在明处，却不判谁赢。

abstract.en: Picture two stacks of paper with a strip of bare wood between them.
abstract.cn: 想象两摞纸之间露出一条空木桌。

abstract.en: Picture two arrows pointing away from one point.
abstract.cn: 想象两个箭头从同一点朝外指去。

abstract.en: Picture two columns of figures that end on different totals.
abstract.cn: 想象两列数字收在不同的总数上。

examples.en: The disagreement was settled before lunch.
examples.cn: 分歧在午饭前就解决了。

examples.en: There is a serious disagreement between the two reports.
examples.cn: 两份报告之间存在严重的出入。

examples.en: They had a disagreement about who should pay.
examples.cn: 他们为该谁付钱发生了争执。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disagreement 记成「的士格瑞闷头」：两个人为了车费在的士里闷头争执，谁也不看谁。

root: 由 dis- 加 agreement 构成。agreement 出自古法语 agreer，源头是拉丁语 gratus（令人愉快的），本指合意与一致。加否定前缀后表示意见分开的状态，后来又引申为由此产生的争执，以及两份记录或数字之间的出入。

sensesIntro.en: From two views that will not meet, to the quarrel that follows, to two records that will not match.
sensesIntro.cn: 从谈不拢的两种看法，到随之而来的争吵，再到对不上的两份记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bare strip of table between two stacks of paper.
core.cn: 核心意象：两摞文件之间露出的那条空桌面。

chain: TWO PEOPLE SIT AT ONE TABLE
THE GAP IS NAMED AND FACED

branches.en: The first sense is the quiet fact of differing views.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是看法不同这件安静的事实。

branches.en: The second sense is the noise that grows out of it.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是由此长出来的声音。

branches.en: The third sense is the gap between things that should match.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是本该相同的两样东西之间的缝。

branches.en: A difference of view and an open quarrel share one root.
branches.cn: 看法不同与公开争吵共有一个根。

branches.en: People and papers both reveal a gap by failing to line up.
branches.cn: 人和纸都靠对不齐来显露那道缝。

intro.en: Disagreement sits in the agree family, beside agreement and disagree.
intro.cn: disagreement 处在 agree 一族里，与 agreement、disagree 相邻。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is gratus, pleasing, which reached English through Old French agreer.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁源头是 gratus（令人愉快），经古法语 agreer 进入英语。

items.meaning: a shared opinion or a formal deal
items.example: They reached an agreement at last.
Both sides agree on the date.

items.exampleCN: 我们度过了一个愉快的晚上。

items.example: He spoke disagreeably to the waiter.
items.exampleCN: 他对服务员说话很难听。

definition_zh: 小巷；窄街；小径；保龄球道；死胡同
definition_en: a narrow passage between buildings, a bowling lane, or a garden path
core_image: 两堵高墙夹出的一条窄缝，尽头才见一点光
scene: 孩子把球滚进两栋楼之间的窄巷，转身就跑。 The cat dashed into a narrow alley between the two buildings.
sceneCN: 这里 alley 是「小巷」（第 1 个义项：建筑之间的狭窄通道）；句意为猫冲进两栋楼之间的窄巷。

pos.zh: 名词：小巷；窄街；小径；保龄球道

derivatives.zh: 由 alley 与 way 构成的复合名词，义为「小巷；窄道」
复合名词，义为「流浪猫」，指在巷子里讨生活的猫
复合名词，义为「保龄球馆」或「保龄球道」
复合名词，义为「死胡同」，也比喻没有前途的办法

senses.title: A narrow passage between buildings
senses.definition: a narrow street or passage running between or behind buildings
senses.definitionCN: 在建筑物之间或后方延伸的狭窄街道或通道
senses.example: They met in an alley behind the market.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在市场后面的一条小巷里见面。
senses.why: Old French alee meant a walking or a passage, from the verb to go; an alley is a route squeezed between walls.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 alee 意为行走或通道，来自表示「走」的动词；alley 就是被墙夹出来的一条路线。

senses.title: A bowling lane
senses.definition: the long narrow track down which a bowling ball is rolled
senses.definitionCN: 供保龄球滚向球瓶的长而窄的球道
senses.example: The ball curved across the alley and hit the last pin.
senses.exampleCN: 球斜穿过球道，击中了最后一只瓶。
senses.why: A bowling lane has exactly the shape of an alley: a long narrow strip with walls or gutters on both sides.
senses.whyCN: 保龄球道的形状正像一条小巷：长而窄，两侧有边沟或挡板。

senses.title: A garden path
senses.definition: a narrow path in a garden or park, often bordered by plants
senses.definitionCN: 花园或公园中的狭窄小径，常由植物镶边
senses.example: A gravel alley led from the gate to the roses.
senses.exampleCN: 一条碎石小径从门口通向玫瑰丛。
senses.why: The passage does not need buildings: any narrow way meant for walking can carry the name.
senses.whyCN: 通道不一定需要建筑：任何供人行走的窄路都能用这个名字。

senses.title: A blind alley: no way forward
senses.definition: a course of action that leads nowhere, from the image of a passage with no exit
senses.definitionCN: 指走不通的做法，来自没有出口的通道这一意象
senses.example: Endless testing was a blind alley for the research team.
senses.exampleCN: 无止境的测试对研究团队来说是条死胡同。
senses.why: A real alley can end at a wall; the mind borrows that wall for any plan that cannot continue.
senses.whyCN: 真实的小巷可以在墙前终止；头脑把那堵墙借给任何无法继续的计划。

intro.en: Alley comes from a French verb meaning to go, and its narrow shape then spread to bowling and to dead ends.
intro.cn: alley 来自一个意为「走」的法语动词，它狭窄的形状随后延伸到保龄球与死胡同。

items.en: Latin ambulare meant to walk about, and it is the distant source of alley and of amble.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ambulare 意为到处走动，是 alley 与 amble 的远源。

items.en: Old French aler meant to go, and its participle alee named a going or a passage.
items.cn: 古法语 aler 意为去、走，其分词形式 alee 指一次行走或一条通道。

items.en: Middle English took the word as aley, a narrow way for walking.
items.cn: 中世纪英语借入作 aley，指供行走的窄路。

items.en: The long narrow lane of a bowling game borrowed the shape and the name.
items.cn: 保龄球那长而窄的球道借用了这个形状，也借用了这个名字。

items.en: Garden paths used the word for any narrow walk bordered by plants.
items.cn: 花园小径用这个词指任何由植物镶边的窄走道。

items.en: The phrase blind alley extended the physical dead end into a failed plan.
items.cn: 短语 blind alley 把物理上的死胡同延伸到失败的计划。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers alley compounds; the near-meaning group gathers narrow ways and passages.
note.cn: 形近组收 alley 的复合词；近义组收狭窄的道路与通道。

entries.definition: A narrow passage, often between buildings.
entries.definitionCN: 指狭窄通道，常在建筑之间。

entries.definition: A stray cat that lives in streets and alleys.
entries.definitionCN: 指在街巷里生活的流浪猫。

entries.definition: A building or lane for bowling.
entries.definitionCN: 指打保龄球的场馆或球道。

entries.definition: A passage with no exit, or a plan that cannot succeed.
entries.definitionCN: 指没有出口的通道，或无法成功的计划。

entries.definition: A narrow road in the country or a marked strip of a wider road.
entries.definitionCN: 指乡间窄路，或宽路上划出的一条车道。

entries.definition: A way through or along which someone or something passes.
entries.definitionCN: 指人或物穿行而过的通道。

entries.definition: A track made by walking, often outdoors.
entries.definitionCN: 指走出来的小路，多在户外。

entries.definition: A long passage inside a building or between rooms.
entries.definitionCN: 指建筑内部或房间之间的长通道。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with the narrow gap and then stretch it into a bowling lane and a dead end.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子先抓住那条窄缝，再把它拉成保龄球道与死胡同。

normal.en: Alley is a walking passage squeezed between two walls, so narrowness is the core.
normal.cn: alley 是被两堵墙夹出来的行走通道，所以「窄」是核心。

normal.en: A bowling alley is an alley laid flat and given pins.
normal.cn: bowling alley 是把小巷放平，再摆上球瓶。

normal.en: A garden alley is the same narrow walk with flowers instead of walls.
normal.cn: 花园小径是同一种窄走道，只是把墙换成了花。

normal.en: A blind alley ends at a wall, so the phrase means a plan that cannot go on.
normal.cn: blind alley 终止于一堵墙，所以这个短语指无法继续的计划。

normal.en: An alley cat lives in the gaps between buildings, not in a house.
normal.cn: alley cat 住在建筑之间的缝隙里，而不是住在屋里。

abstract.en: Picture two high brick walls almost touching, with a thin strip of sky above them.
abstract.cn: 想象两堵高高的砖墙几乎相碰，上方只留一条细细的天空。

abstract.en: Lay the strip down horizontally and it becomes a lane with a ball rolling along it.
abstract.cn: 把这条缝横过来放平，它就成了一条有球滚过的球道。

abstract.en: Put a wall across the far end and the same strip becomes a blind alley.
abstract.cn: 在远端横上一堵墙，同一条缝就成了死胡同。

examples.en: The delivery van blocked the narrow alley behind the shop.
examples.cn: 送货的面包车堵住了商店后面的窄巷。

examples.en: They spent the afternoon at a bowling alley near the station.
examples.cn: 他们一下午都待在车站附近的保龄球馆。

examples.en: The committee realized the old plan was a blind alley.
examples.cn: 委员会意识到旧方案是一条死胡同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱理」——爱理不理，只肯走那条没人理的小巷

root: 经由古法语 alee（行走、通道）来自拉丁语 ambulare（走动）；本指两墙之间的窄路，后引申指保龄球道、花园小径，并以 blind alley 比喻无出路的办法。

sensesIntro.en: The four senses all keep the shape of a long narrow strip, filled with walls, gutters, plants, or a final barrier.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项都保留「长而窄的一条」这个形状，只是填进去的是墙、边沟、植物或一道终点屏障。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two walls stand almost touching, and a thin line of light runs between them toward the far end.
core.cn: 核心意象：两堵墙几乎相贴，一线光在它们之间一直延伸到远端。

branches.en: THE GAP: the first sense is a way for people squeezed between buildings.
branches.cn: 缝隙线：第一个义项是人们在建筑之间挤过去的路。

branches.en: THE LANE: the same strip lies flat and becomes a track for a rolling ball.
branches.cn: 球道线：同一条窄带放平，就成了滚球的轨道。

branches.en: THE GARDEN: walls give way to plants, but the narrow walk remains.
branches.cn: 花园线：墙换成了植物，窄走道仍然保留。

branches.en: THE WALL: when the far end is closed, the passage becomes a metaphor for failure.
branches.cn: 墙线：远端被封住时，通道就成了失败的比喻。

branches.en: THE HIDDEN WAY: an alley is often a route people use to avoid the main street.
branches.cn: 暗线：小巷常是人们避开主街时走的路线。

intro.en: Alley is a French loanword with a small family built by compounding rather than suffixation.
intro.cn: alley 是法语借词，小词族靠复合构词而不是后缀派生。

latinIntro.en: The word goes back to Latin ambulare, but it entered English through French, so the Latin entries are indirect.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词上溯至拉丁语 ambulare，但经法语进入英语，因此拉丁条目是间接的。

items.example: The alley was too narrow for a car.
items.exampleCN: 这条小巷窄得车开不进去。

items.example: It is the distant source of alley.

items.exampleCN: 它的分词形式产生了 alee。

items.example: They walked through a dark alleyway.
items.exampleCN: 他们穿过一条黑暗的窄道。

items.example: An alley cat slept on the bins.
items.exampleCN: 一只流浪猫睡在垃圾桶上。

items.meaning: a place or lane for bowling
items.example: The bowling alley was full on Friday.
The route ended in a blind alley.
items.exampleCN: 这条路线终止在一条死胡同里。

definition_en: in a general way, without details
core_image: 从高处俯看一整片区域
scene: 两张方案摊在桌上。 Broadly speaking, the two plans cost the same.
sceneCN: 这里 broadly 是「大体上」（第 1 个义项：不涉及细节地）；句意是大体上说，两个方案花费相同。

derivatives.zh: 宽的；广泛的，broadly 的词基

senses.title: In general terms
senses.definition: considered in a general way rather than in detail
senses.definitionCN: 从大处看，不涉及细节
senses.example: Broadly speaking, the two plans cost the same.
senses.exampleCN: 大体上说，两个方案花费相同。
senses.why: A wide view sees the whole shape before the small parts.
senses.whyCN: 宽阔的视野先看到整体轮廓，再看细小部分。

senses.title: Over a wide range
senses.definition: in a way that covers many kinds or areas
senses.definitionCN: 涵盖许多种类或领域
senses.example: The course is broadly based on real cases.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课广泛地以真实案例为基础。
senses.why: The adverb keeps the physical idea of spreading wide.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词保留了「铺得很开」的物理意象。

senses.title: With a wide smile
senses.definition: with the mouth open wide in a smile
senses.definitionCN: 笑得嘴张得很开
senses.example: She smiled broadly at the good news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到好消息，她咧开嘴笑了。
senses.why: A wide mouth and a wide space share the same image of breadth.
senses.whyCN: 张大的嘴与宽阔的空间共有「宽度」这一形象。

intro.en: Broadly is broad plus the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: broadly 是 broad 加副词后缀 -ly。

items.en: brād meant wide, and -līce made adverbs from adjectives.
items.cn: brād 意为宽，-līce 把形容词变成副词。

items.en: The two parts merged into the adverb broadly.
items.cn: 两部分合成了副词 broadly。

items.en: Broadly began to mean plainly or openly.
items.cn: broadly 开始表示明白地、公开地。

items.en: Broadly speaking became a set phrase in argument.
items.cn: broadly speaking 成为议论中的固定说法。

items.en: Broadly marks a general statement or a wide smile.
items.cn: 如今 broadly 标记概括的说法或咧开的笑。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the broad- stem; the near-meaning group gives other general adverbs.
note.cn: 形近组共用 broad- 词干；近义组是其他表示概括的副词。

normalIntro.en: Broadly turns the width of broad into a way of speaking.
normalIntro.cn: broadly 把 broad 的宽度变成一种说话方式。

normal.en: Broadly speaking means in general.
normal.cn: broadly speaking 的意思是大体上说。

normal.en: Two broadly similar things differ only in detail.
normal.cn: broadly similar 指只在细节上有差别。

normal.en: The adverb adds -ly to broad.
normal.cn: 这个副词由 broad 加 -ly 构成。

normal.en: A broadly based group draws from many places.
normal.cn: broadly based 指来自许多地方。

normal.en: To smile broadly is to smile wide.
normal.cn: smile broadly 就是咧开嘴笑。

abstract.en: See a whole city from a high window.
abstract.cn: 想象从高窗俯看整座城市。

abstract.en: See a net thrown over a wide area.
abstract.cn: 想象一张网撒得很开。

abstract.en: See a mouth opening into a wide grin.
abstract.cn: 想象一张嘴咧成一个大笑。

examples.en: Broadly speaking, the two plans cost the same.
examples.cn: 大体上说，两个方案花费相同。

examples.en: The course is broadly based on real cases.
examples.cn: 这门课广泛地以真实案例为基础。

examples.en: She smiled broadly at the good news.
examples.cn: 听到好消息，她咧开嘴笑了。

dict_mnemonic.text: broad 是宽，-ly 是「以……方式」，用宽的方式看事情，就是大体上。

root: broadly 由古英语 brād（宽）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，先表示公开、明白，后固定为「大体上」，也保留了「铺得广」「咧得开」的形象。

sensesIntro.en: Seeing the outline, covering many areas, and smiling wide.
sensesIntro.cn: 看整体轮廓、覆盖许多方面、把嘴咧得很开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole city seen from a high window.
core.cn: 核心意象：从高窗俯看整座城市。

branches.en: broadly speaking
branches.cn: 大体上说

branches.en: broadly similar
branches.cn: 大体相似的

branches.en: broadly based
branches.cn: 基础广泛的

branches.en: broadly agree
branches.cn: 大致同意

branches.en: smile broadly
branches.cn: 咧开嘴笑

intro.en: Broadly is an -ly adverb built on the adjective broad.
intro.cn: broadly 是由形容词 broad 加 -ly 构成的副词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Old English; the Latin items below are related only in meaning.
latinIntro.cn: 词基来自古英语，下面的拉丁词只在意思上相关。

definition_en: to change your appearance so that people do not know you, or to hide a feeling or fact
core_image: 镜子里的人贴上一副假胡子，几乎认不出自己
scene: 他对着镜子贴上一副假胡子，连自己都愣了一下。 She disguised herself as a nurse to enter the ward.
sceneCN: 这里 disguise 指「伪装」（第 1 个义项：改变外表使人认不出）；句意是她扮成护士进了病房。

senses.title: To change how you look
senses.definition: to change your appearance so that people cannot recognize you
senses.definitionCN: 改变外表让人认不出你
senses.example: She disguised herself as a nurse.
senses.exampleCN: 她扮成护士。
senses.why: A face is a door, and a false beard is a new key.
senses.whyCN: 脸是一扇门，假胡子是一把新钥匙。

senses.title: To hide a feeling or fact
senses.definition: to hide something such as a feeling or a fact
senses.definitionCN: 把情感或事实遮盖起来
senses.example: He could not disguise his anger.
senses.exampleCN: 他掩饰不住怒气。
senses.why: What is covered still shows at the corners of the mouth.
senses.whyCN: 被盖住的东西，仍会从嘴角露出来。

intro.en: Disguise comes from Old French desguisier, where des- reversed a guise, a manner or dress.
intro.cn: disguise 来自古法语 desguisier，前缀 des- 把 guise（样子、装束）反过来。

items.en: Wisa meant manner or way, and reached French as guise.
items.cn: wisa 指方式、样子，进入法语成为 guise。

items.en: Desguisier meant to change the usual manner or dress.
items.cn: 古法语 desguisier 指改变平常的样子或装束。

items.en: English used it for a false dress or appearance.
items.cn: 英语借入后指虚假的装束或外表。

items.en: The noun added the thing worn as a cover.
items.cn: 名词又添上用来遮盖的物件这一义。

items.en: The word now also hides feelings, not only faces.
items.cn: 今天它不只遮脸，也遮情绪。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the guise stem, and the meaning group gathers other ways of covering.
note.cn: 形近组保留 guise 词干，近义组聚起别的遮掩方式。

entries.definition: a way of appearing or behaving
to make something blend into its setting
entries.definitionCN: 使融入环境而不被看见

entries.definition: to keep something from being seen

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a false beard in a mirror and end with a feeling that still shows.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从镜前一副假胡子开始，落到一种仍会露出来的情绪。

normal.en: Dis- plus guise: the usual guise is changed.
normal.cn: dis 加 guise，把平常的样子换掉。

normal.en: A guard in an old coat can walk past any gate.
normal.cn: 穿旧大衣的警卫能走过任何一道门。

normal.en: A blessing in disguise hides its good side at first.
normal.cn: 因祸得福的事，起初把好的一面藏起来。

normal.en: A thin smile cannot disguise a tired voice.
normal.cn: 淡淡的笑掩不住疲惫的声音。

normal.en: A fact disguised is still a fact in the room.
normal.cn: 被掩饰的事实，仍留在屋子里。

abstract.en: Picture a false beard stuck on in a mirror.
abstract.cn: 想象对着镜子贴上一副假胡子。

abstract.en: Picture a coat turned inside out.
abstract.cn: 想象一件大衣被翻过来穿。

abstract.en: Picture a smile held a moment too long.
abstract.cn: 想象一个笑得稍久了一点。

examples.en: She disguised herself as a nurse to enter the ward.
examples.cn: 她扮成护士进了病房。

examples.en: He could not disguise his disappointment.
examples.cn: 他掩饰不住失望。

examples.en: The delay turned out to be a blessing in disguise.
examples.cn: 这次延误后来倒成了因祸得福。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disguise 记成「换一副样子」：dis 表示改变，guise 是样子，把平常的样子换掉，就是伪装。

root: 来自古法语 desguisier，由 des-（改变、反转）与 guise（样子、装束）构成，guise 又可追到日耳曼语 wisa（方式）。本义是改变平常的装束与举止，后来也从遮脸引申为遮掩情感与事实。

sensesIntro.en: From a face made strange to a feeling that will not stay covered.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一张被改得陌生的脸，到一种盖不住的情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a false beard pasted on in front of a mirror.
core.cn: 核心意象：镜前贴上一副假胡子。

branches.en: The first sense is the body made unrecognizable.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是身体被改得认不出。

branches.en: The second sense moves the cover inward, onto feeling.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把遮盖挪进心里，盖住情绪。

branches.en: Both senses put something false in front of the true thing.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在真东西前面放一层假的。

branches.en: Both work best when nobody looks twice.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在没人多看第二眼时最管用。

branches.en: Only the second sense can be done with a single smile.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项能靠一个微笑完成。

intro.en: Disguise sits in the guise family, where a manner or dress can be put on and taken off.
intro.cn: disguise 属于 guise 一族，样子与装束可以穿上，也可以脱下。

latinIntro.en: Old French guise, a manner, gives English guise and disguise, with des- turning the manner against itself.
latinIntro.cn: 古法语 guise（样子）给出英语 guise 与 disguise，前缀 des- 让样子背离自身。

items.example: They disguised the van as a van of flowers.
items.exampleCN: 他们把货车伪装成运花的车。

items.example: He came in the guise of a friend.
A disguised door stood in the wall.
Her undisguised joy filled the room.
items.exampleCN: 她毫不掩饰的喜悦充满房间。

items.meaning: the act of hiding by appearance

items.example: The offer came guised as help.
items.exampleCN: 这个提议以帮助的样子出现。
那场聚会是一场假面舞会。

items.meaning: a cover that blends with the ground

definition_en: the straps and bands used to control a horse, or to control and use a force
core_image: 皮带与铜扣把一匹马稳稳系在车辕上
scene: 农民给马套上马具。 The farmer put the harness on the horse.
sceneCN: 这里 harness 是「马具」（第 1 个义项）；句意：农民给马套上马具。

senses.title: Straps for an animal
senses.definition: the set of straps used to tie an animal to a cart or plough
senses.definitionCN: 把牲畜系在车或犁上的一套皮带
senses.example: The farmer put the harness on the horse.
senses.exampleCN: 农民给马套上马具。
senses.why: This is the basic object sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的实物义项。

senses.title: Put a force to work
senses.definition: to control and use a natural force for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为某种目的控制和利用自然力
senses.example: The dam harnesses the river.
senses.exampleCN: 大坝利用着这条河的力量。
senses.why: Straps that control a horse came to control power.
senses.whyCN: 控制马的皮带，变成了控制力量的手段。

senses.title: Strap an animal
senses.definition: to fasten a harness onto an animal
senses.definitionCN: 把马具系到牲畜身上
senses.example: They harnessed the horses at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在黎明时给马套上马具。
senses.why: The noun of straps became the act of strapping.
senses.whyCN: 皮带的名词，转成了系皮带这个动作。

intro.en: Harness comes from Old French harneis, equipment for a horse or soldier.
intro.cn: harness 来自古法语 harneis，指马匹或士兵的装备。

items.en: Harneis meant military equipment.
items.cn: harneis 意为军事装备。

items.en: Harness named the gear of a horse.
items.cn: harness 指马的挽具。

items.en: The verb named putting on the gear.
items.cn: 动词义指给牲口套上挽具。

items.en: Harness extended to water and wind.
items.cn: harness 扩展到水力与风力。

items.en: It now names using any great power.
items.cn: 现在它指利用任何巨大的力量。

note.en: Harness is compared with look-alike words and with words for using power.
note.cn: 把 harness 与形近词以及表示利用力量的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Harness is leather on a horse, then leather on a river of power.
normalIntro.cn: harness 先是套在马身上的皮带，后来套在力量之河上。

normal.en: The horse wore a leather harness.
normal.cn: 马戴着皮制挽具。

normal.en: Wind farms harness the air.
normal.cn: 风电场利用空气的力量。

normal.en: We can harness sunlight for heat.
normal.cn: 我们可以利用阳光取暖。

normal.en: The climber wore a safety harness.
normal.cn: 登山者系着安全带。

normal.en: They harnessed the team to one goal.
normal.cn: 他们把团队的力量汇到一个目标上。

abstract.en: Power becomes useful only when it is held.
abstract.cn: 力量只有被握住，才有用处。

abstract.en: A wild river and a wild will both need a harness.
abstract.cn: 野河与野性，都需要一副挽具。

abstract.en: To harness is to listen to force before using it.
abstract.cn: 驾驭，是先听懂力量，再使用它。

examples.en: The farmer put the harness on the horse.
examples.cn: 农民给马套上马具。

examples.en: The dam harnesses the river.
examples.cn: 大坝利用着这条河的力量。

examples.en: They harnessed the horses at dawn.
examples.cn: 他们在黎明时给马套上马具。

dict_mnemonic.text: harness 本指马的「挽具」，把马系住才能干活，于是动词引申为「利用」自然力，如 harness solar energy 是利用太阳能；safety harness 是安全带。

root: 来自古法语 harneis（装备）；由给马套挽具，引申为控制并利用水力、风力、太阳能等巨大力量。

sensesIntro.en: Harness is gear for an animal, the use of a great force, or the act of strapping up.
sensesIntro.cn: harness 是牲畜的挽具、对巨大力量的利用，或套上挽具的动作。

core.en: Leather straps that hold a strong animal.
core.cn: 系住强壮牲畜的皮带。

branches.en: Buckled straps cross a horse's back.
branches.cn: 带扣的皮带横过马背。

branches.en: Water turns a wheel and lights a town.
branches.cn: 水推动轮子，点亮小镇。

branches.en: Hands buckle a collar before sunrise.
branches.cn: 日出前，双手扣上颈圈。

branches.en: The gear and the strapping are one action seen twice.
branches.cn: 挽具与套挽具，是同一动作的两种看法。

branches.en: To control a horse became to control a river.
branches.cn: 控制一匹马，变成了控制一条河。

intro.en: Harness takes plural and verb endings and forms gear compounds.
intro.cn: harness 加复数与动词词尾，并构成装备类复合词。

latinIntro.en: The word comes from Old French, not from Latin roots.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词来自古法语，并非拉丁词根。

items.example: The river is harnessed for power.
The team is back in harness.

items.exampleCN: 他们重新利用了老磨坊。

definition_zh: 不仁慈的；不厚道的；刻薄的；不体贴的
definition_en: behaving in a way that is cruel, cold, or hurtful to others
core_image: 伸出去的手被干脆地拨开
scene: 她递东西给父亲，父亲头也没回低声说了句让她走开。 It was unkind of him to say that.
sceneCN: 这里 unkind 是「刻薄的、不厚道的」（第 1 个义项：待人冷酷伤人）；句意为他那样说太不厚道。伸出的手被干脆拨开，正是这个词的核心画面。

collocations.phrase: it is unkind of someone to

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「刻薄地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「刻薄；不仁」
去掉否定前缀的形容词，义为「善良的；和善的」
肯定形式的名词，义为「善意；亲切」

senses.title: Cruel or cold in words
senses.definition: saying things that are hard, cold, or hurtful
senses.definitionCN: 说出冷酷伤人、不近情理的话
senses.example: It was unkind to laugh at his mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 嘲笑他的错误太刻薄了。
senses.why: The prefix denies kind, and kind comes from the old word for one family, so unkind is treating someone as a stranger.
senses.whyCN: 前缀否定了 kind，而 kind 本出自「同族」的古义，所以 unkind 就是把人当作外人对待。

senses.title: Hard in action, not only in words
senses.definition: acting in a way that ignores another person trouble
senses.definitionCN: 做事时全然不顾别人的难处
senses.example: It was unkind of them to leave her standing in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把她丢在雨里站着，实在不厚道。
senses.why: Whatever denies kin denies the help kin deserve, so the word covers deeds as well as speech.
senses.whyCN: 否定「同类」也就否定了同类应得的照料，所以这个词兼指言与行。

senses.title: Chilling an atmosphere
senses.definition: used of treatment that shows no warmth or care
senses.definitionCN: 形容毫无暖意与关照的对待
senses.example: The unkind treatment she met at the front desk upset her all day.
senses.exampleCN: 她在前台受到的冷遇让她难受了一整天。
senses.why: Hard words repeated become an atmosphere, and the adjective follows them there.
senses.whyCN: 刻薄的话反复出现就成了气氛，这个形容词也随之延伸过去。

senses.title: Harsh in its effects
senses.titleCN: 苛刻的；不近人情的（评判）
senses.definition: used of a judgement or condition that shows no mercy
senses.definitionCN: 形容毫不留情的评判或处境
senses.example: The review of her first book was unkind but fair.
senses.exampleCN: 对她第一本书的评论很苛刻，却也公道。
senses.why: A judgement that considers no one feelings repeats the same lack of kin.
senses.whyCN: 不顾任何人感受的评判，重复着同样的「不认同类」。

senses.title: Against the nature of something
senses.definition: in older use, used of a climate or soil that does not suit a plant
senses.definitionCN: 较古用法，形容气候或土壤不适于某种草木
senses.example: They planted the vine where the soil was unkind to it.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把葡萄种在土质不适合它生长的地方。
senses.why: Being unsuited to a plant is the same denial of kind, moved from people to soil.
senses.whyCN: 不适宜草木，仍是同一种对 kind 的否定，只是从人挪到了土壤。

intro.en: Kind is an old English word for nature and family, and the negative prefix reverses its warmth.
intro.cn: kind 是古英语中表示「天性、同族」的词，否定前缀把那份暖意反了过来。

items.en: Gecynd meant nature or race, and cynde meant natural or well-born.
items.cn: gecynd 意为天性、族类，cynde 意为本性的、出身好的。

items.en: Kind came to mean well-disposed, then warm and considerate.
items.cn: kind 转为表示「心性好的」，再变为「温和体贴的」。

items.en: Un- was prefixed to kind to name the opposite temper.
items.cn: 在 kind 前加 un-，用来命名相反的性情。

items.en: Unkind was applied first to words and looks, then to deeds.
items.cn: unkind 先用于言语神情，再扩展到行为。

items.en: The older sense survives in kind as a noun for a sort or type.
items.cn: 较古的「种类」之义仍存于名词 kind 之中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers kind forms, and the near-meaning group covers cruel words.
note.cn: 形近组收集 kind 的各个形式，近义组覆盖与刻薄残忍相关的词。

entries.definition: in a warm and caring way
in a cold and hurtful way

entries.definitionCN: 放松；解开（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

normalIntro.en: The word denies kinship: someone who is unkind treats you as though you were not one of us.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词否定的是「同类」：不厚道的人把你当作外人。

normal.en: Un- plus kind: without the warmth owed to kin.
normal.cn: un- 加 kind：没有那份对同类该有的暖意。

normal.en: Be unkind to someone and it is unkind to do are the two frames.
normal.cn: be unkind to someone 与 It is unkind to do 是两个常用句型。

normal.en: Kind also means type, as in a kind of bird.
normal.cn: kind 还有「种类」之义，如 a kind of bird。

normal.en: Unkindly is the adverb, unkindness the noun.
normal.cn: 副词是 unkindly，名词是 unkindness。

normal.en: Unkind is gentler than cruel; it judges manner rather than intent.
normal.cn: unkind 比 cruel 轻，评的是态度而非蓄意伤害。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reached out that is simply brushed away.
abstract.cn: 想象伸出去的手被干脆拨开。

abstract.en: See a child told to go away in a flat voice.
abstract.cn: 看孩子被一个平板的声调赶走。

abstract.en: Hear laughter that starts before the joke ends.
abstract.cn: 听笑声在笑话结束前就先响起来。

examples.en: It was unkind to point out the mistake in front of everyone.
examples.cn: 当众指出那个错误，太不厚道。

examples.en: She never said an unkind word about her neighbours.
examples.cn: 她从没说过邻居一句刻薄话。

examples.en: He treated the new pupil unkindly at first and regretted it later.
examples.cn: 他起初对那个转学生很刻薄，后来后悔了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺砍的」——话说得像刀砍一样，一刀一刀割在人心上，太不厚道。

root: 前缀 un-（不）+ kind，kind 源自古英语 cynde/gecynd（天性、族类），由「同族、本性」转义为「和善」

sensesIntro.en: One denial of kinship runs from a cold remark to a harsh review and even to unsuitable soil.
sensesIntro.cn: 一次对「同类」的否定，从冷言冷语延伸到苛刻评论，乃至不宜的土壤。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an offered hand brushed away.
core.cn: 核心意象：递出的手被一把拨开。

branches.en: The word branch: jokes and remarks that cut.
branches.cn: 言语分支：伤人的玩笑与话。

branches.en: The deed branch: leaving someone in the rain.
branches.cn: 行为分支：把某人丢在雨里。

branches.en: The atmosphere branch: treatment with no warmth.
branches.cn: 气氛分支：毫无暖意的对待。

branches.en: The judgement branch: a review without mercy.
branches.cn: 评判分支：毫不留情的评论。

branches.en: The natural branch: soil that does not suit a plant.
branches.cn: 自然分支：不宜草木的土壤。

intro.en: The parts are a negative prefix and a very old native adjective.
intro.cn: 部件是否定前缀与一个极古的本土形容词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin layer; kind is Germanic, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁语层，kind 属日耳曼语，因此拉丁词条留空。

items.example: Her kindness was remembered for years.
items.exampleCN: 她的善意被人记了很多年。

items.example: A cruel word can last a lifetime.
items.exampleCN: 一句残忍的话能记一辈子。

items.example: A thoughtless remark spoiled the evening.
items.exampleCN: 一句不体谅的话毁了这个晚上。

definition_en: not following accepted standards of right and wrong behaviour
core_image: 办公室里有人把公家的东西悄悄塞进自己的背包
scene: 加班的晚上只剩他一个人，柜门开着。 Taking the printer home felt immoral to everyone in the department, though nothing in the handbook forbade it.
sceneCN: 这里 immoral 是「不道德的」（第 1 个义项：违背公认是非标准），句意是部门里人人都觉得把打印机拿回家不道德，尽管手册上没有禁止。画面里有独自加班的人、开着的柜门和塞进背包的东西。

pos.zh: 形容词：不道德的、违背道德的

senses.title: Against accepted standards of right
senses.definition: contrary to the moral rules a community holds
senses.definitionCN: 违背一个群体所持的道德准则
senses.example: Cheating poor customers is simply immoral.
senses.exampleCN: 欺骗穷顾客简直就是不道德的。
senses.why: The prefix is a straightforward negative on the Latin word for custom, so the word means against the mores of a community.
senses.whyCN: 前缀是对拉丁语「习俗」一词的直白否定，因此这个词意为违背共同体的风气与准则。

senses.title: Wrong even if legal
senses.definition: used to judge conduct that the law permits but conscience rejects
senses.definitionCN: 用来评判法律容许而良心反对的行为
senses.example: It may be legal to sell the drug, but many find it immoral.
senses.exampleCN: 卖这种药也许合法，但很多人认为不正当。
senses.why: Because the word answers to custom rather than statute, it can condemn what courts allow.
senses.whyCN: 由于这个词依据的是风气而非法条，它能谴责法院所容许的事。

senses.title: Used of gains and profits
senses.definition: describing money earned in a way that harms others
senses.definitionCN: 形容以损害他人方式赚来的钱
senses.example: They refused immoral profits from the trade.
senses.exampleCN: 他们拒绝从这门生意中获取不义之财。
senses.why: Gain is the commonest test case of morality, so the adjective attaches readily to profit and money.
senses.whyCN: 利益是道德最常见的试金石，于是这个形容词常与利润、钱财搭配。

intro.en: Immoral negatives a Latin word for custom and manners; oddly, the positive word moral is younger in English usage.
intro.cn: immoral 是对拉丁语「习俗、风气」一词的否定；有趣的是，肯定式 moral 在英语里出现得反而更晚。

items.en: Mos, plural mores, meant custom or manner, the unwritten habits of a people.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mos（复数 mores）意为习俗、风气，即一个民族不成文的习惯。

items.en: Moralis was coined to describe what concerns such customs, and later what concerns right conduct.
items.cn: moralis 被用来形容与此类习俗相关之事，后来转为涉及正当行为。

items.en: French morale kept the sense of conduct and character.
items.cn: 法语 morale 保留行为与品格之意。

items.en: Immoral was used in English before moral settled, naming conduct against accepted custom.
items.cn: immoral 在 moral 定形之前就已在英语中使用，指违背公认习俗的行为。

items.en: Victorian debate sharpened the word, and it became a standard charge in law, church and press.
items.cn: 维多利亚时代的争论使这个词更锋利，成了法律、教会与报纸的标准指控。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the moral family; the near-meaning group gathers other words of blame.
note.cn: 形近组收 moral 词族；近义组收其他表示指责的词。

entries.definition: Lacking moral sense altogether, rather than acting against it.
entries.definitionCN: 根本没有道德观念，而非有意违背。

entries.definition: Concerned with right behaviour; the base word.
entries.definitionCN: 涉及是非行为的，本词的原形。

entries.definition: The quality of being immoral, or an immoral act.
entries.definitionCN: 不道德的性质，或不道德的行为。

entries.definition: Against the rules of a profession or business, less about personal conscience.
entries.definitionCN: 违背行业规范，较少涉及个人良心。

entries.definition: Morally very bad, with a stronger emotional charge.
entries.definitionCN: 道德上极坏，情感色彩更重。

entries.definition: Willing to do wrong to get what one wants.

normalIntro.en: The hooks separate immoral from amoral and tie the word to custom rather than law.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把 immoral 与 amoral 分开，并把词义系在风气而非法律上。

normal.en: Im- is not, moral is right conduct: not right.
normal.cn: im- 是不，moral 是正当行为：也就是「不正当」。

normal.en: Immoral would mislead you, so keep a single m after the prefix: im-moral.
normal.cn: 别误写成 imm moral，前缀之后只有一个 m：im-moral。

normal.en: Three beats, stress the middle: im-MOR-al.
normal.cn: 三个拍子，重音在中间：im-MOR-al。

normal.en: Amoral removes the fault, immoral charges it; the prefix tells you which.
normal.cn: amoral 抽掉了过错，immoral 指控过错，换个前缀就换了态度。

normal.en: Moral came from mores, the customs people honour; the word judges against a community.
normal.cn: moral 源自 mores（人们遵守的习俗），这个词是拿共同体的标准来评判。

abstract.en: The word speaks in the voice of a community, so arguments about it rarely settle on facts alone.
abstract.cn: 这个词用共同体的声音说话，因此关于它的争论很少只靠事实了结。

abstract.en: Something legal can still be immoral, and that gap is where most of our hardest questions live.
abstract.cn: 合法之事仍可能不道德，我们最难的问题大多住在这道缝隙里。

abstract.en: Immoral names a broken custom, not a broken law, so the accused may never see a judge.
abstract.cn: immoral 命名的是被破坏的风俗，而非被违反的法条，被告也许永远见不到法官。

examples.en: Many workers thought the pay cut was immoral.
examples.cn: 许多工人认为降薪不道德。

examples.en: He was condemned for immoral conduct in office.
examples.cn: 他因任职期间不道德的行为而受到谴责。

examples.en: There is nothing immoral about asking for help.
examples.cn: 寻求帮助没有任何不道德之处。

dict_mnemonic.text: im 不 + moral 道德的——不道德的；注意与 amoral（无道德意识的）分开

root: 拉丁语 mos（复数 mores）「习俗、风气」→ moralis「与习俗相关的」，加否定前缀 in-（在 m 前作 im-）构成 immoral。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: against community custom, wrong though legal, and used of gains.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：违背群体习俗、合法但不正当，以及用于钱财的「不义」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: office goods slipped quietly into a private bag at night.
core.cn: 核心意象：夜里把公家物件悄悄塞进私人背包。

branches.en: THE NEIGHBOUR LINE: the community's standards do the judging.
branches.cn: 邻里线：由共同体的标准来评判。

branches.en: THE LAW LINE: the word can stand outside the statute book.
branches.cn: 法律线：这个词可以站在法典之外。

branches.en: THE MONEY LINE: tainted profits are its favourite target.
branches.cn: 金钱线：不义之财是它最常针对的对象。

branches.en: THE CONSCIENCE LINE: both senses appeal to an inner court.
branches.cn: 良心线：两种用法都诉诸一个内心的法庭。

branches.en: THE CONTRAST LINE: moral and amoral sit on either side as counterwords.
branches.cn: 对照线：moral 与 amoral 分立两侧，构成反衬。

intro.en: Immoral is the negative of a Latin custom word, with a small family that includes its mild look-alike amoral.
intro.cn: immoral 是拉丁语「习俗」词的否定形，同族中还有容易混淆的 amoral。

latinIntro.en: Mos, mores and moralis are recorded in Latin; the prefix im- is in- assimilated before m.
latinIntro.cn: mos、mores 与 moralis 均有拉丁文献；前缀 im- 是 in- 在 m 前的同化形式。

items.example: Mores is the same root as a Latin plural.
items.exampleCN: mores 正是该词根的拉丁复数形式。

items.example: Natural and legal use it too.
The deal was widely called immoral.
items.exampleCN: 这笔交易被普遍称为不道德。

items.meaningCN: 一般不用比较级，作绝对判断
items.example: Most people called it simply immoral.

items.meaning: the state or an act of being immoral
items.exampleCN: 该报抨击官员的不道德行为。
他们行事不道德却合法。

items.example: A machine is amoral, not immoral.
items.exampleCN: 机器无所谓不道德，它没有道德意识。

definition_en: the sound of many people clapping to show approval, or praise for an achievement
core_image: 剧场里忽然响起的一整片掌声
scene: 最后一个音落下，灯亮起，观众一齐抬起手。 The audience burst into applause.
sceneCN: 这里 applause 是「掌声」（第 1 个义项：观众拍手表示的赞许）；句意是观众爆发出掌声。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：似乎合理的，与 applause 同源于「拍手」

senses.title: Clapping to show approval
senses.definition: the noise made by a group of people clapping their hands in praise
senses.definitionCN: 一群人拍手表示赞赏所发出的声音
senses.example: The audience burst into applause.
senses.exampleCN: 观众爆发出掌声。
senses.why: Latin applaudere joined ad, 'to', and plaudere, 'to clap', so applause is literally clapping toward a performer.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 applaudere 由 ad「向」与 plaudere「拍手」构成，所以 applause 字面就是朝表演者拍手。

senses.title: Public praise
senses.definition: spoken or written approval for a person's achievement
senses.definitionCN: 对某人成就的口头或书面赞许
senses.example: The policy won applause from both sides.
senses.exampleCN: 这项政策赢得了双方的赞许。
senses.why: Clapping is approval made audible, so the same noun can name approval even when no hands are moving.
senses.whyCN: 鼓掌是听得见的赞许，所以同一个名词也能指无人拍手时的赞同。

intro.en: Applause comes from a Latin verb meaning 'to clap towards'.
intro.cn: applause 来自拉丁语中意为「朝……拍手」的动词。

items.en: ad meant 'to, towards'.
items.cn: ad 意为「向」。

items.en: plaudere meant 'to clap the hands'.
items.cn: plaudere 意为「拍手」。

items.en: applaudere meant 'to clap in approval'.
items.cn: applaudere 意为「拍手表示赞许」。

items.en: applausus was the noun for the clapping itself.
items.cn: applausus 是表示拍手这一行为的名词。

items.en: English applause kept the noun while the verb became applaud.
items.cn: 英语保留名词 applause，动词则作 applaud。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the clap root; the near-meaning group gives other signs of approval.
note.cn: 形近组共享「拍手」词根；近义组是其他表示赞许的方式。

entries.definition: seeming reasonable, from the same clap
entries.definitionCN: 似乎合理的，同源于「拍手」

entries.definition: to burst out, from clapping off a stage
entries.definitionCN: 爆炸，同源于「拍手赶下台」

normalIntro.en: Applause is clapping sent toward the stage.
normalIntro.cn: applause 就是朝舞台送去的拍手声。

normal.en: A round of applause is one burst of clapping.
normal.cn: a round of applause 指一阵掌声。

normal.en: The verb is applaud; applause is the noun.
normal.cn: 动词是 applaud，名词是 applause。

normal.en: Thunderous applause describes very loud clapping.
normal.cn: thunderous applause 形容极响的掌声。

normal.en: Applause is uncountable: say a round of applause, not an applause.
normal.cn: applause 不可数，应说 a round of applause，不说 an applause。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: a-PPLAUSE.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：a-PPLAUSE。

abstract.en: See a hall of raised hands in the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗中一片举起的手。

abstract.en: See a conductor turning to bow.
abstract.cn: 想象指挥转身鞠躬。

abstract.en: See a curtain call under warm lights.
abstract.cn: 想象暖光下的谢幕。

examples.en: The audience burst into applause.
examples.cn: 观众爆发出掌声。

examples.en: The policy won applause from both sides.
examples.cn: 这项政策赢得了双方的赞许。

examples.en: She waited for the applause to die down.
examples.cn: 她等着掌声平息下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: ap-（向）加 plaud（拍手）：朝台上拍手，就是掌声。

root: 来自拉丁语 applausus，源于 applaudere「拍手赞许」，由 ad「向」与 plaudere「拍手」构成；动词形式为 applaud。

sensesIntro.en: Audible clapping and spoken approval are two forms of the same praise.
sensesIntro.cn: 听得见的拍手与说出口的赞许，是同一种赞赏的两种形态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many hands striking together at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多只手同时拍响。

branches.cn: 一阵掌声

branches.cn: 雷鸣般的掌声

branches.en: polite applause
branches.cn: 礼貌性的掌声

branches.cn: 赢得赞许

branches.cn: 对改革的赞许

intro.cn: 这是一个表示拍手的拉丁名词，英语另有对应的动词。
